items.title: Chow lemma for separated finite-type morphisms over a Noetherian base
items.published_title: Chow lemma for separated finite-type morphisms over a Noetherian base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a quasi-projective proper modification of a separated finite-type scheme over a Noetherian base using closures of diagonal graph maps. Scheme-theoretic density permits gluing the local projections and proves exact inverse-image identities; these verify properness, surjectivity and a dense-open isomorphism. This is a substantive geometric construction beyond routine qualifying algebra.

research_reviews.difficulty_reason:
题面（源 coherent.tex statement_lines=[4922, 4940] = b8-dump.txt:2911-2929，label=lemma-chow-Noetherian，env=lemma）：设 $S$ 为 Noetherian scheme，$f : X \to S$ 为 separated 且 finite type 的态射。断言：存在 $n \geq 0$ 与图表（原文照抄）
$$
\xymatrix{
X \ar[rd] & X' \ar[d] \ar[l]^\pi \ar[r] & \mathbf{P}^n_S \ar[dl] \\
& S &
}
$$
"where $X' \to \mathbf{P}^n_S$ is an immersion, and $\pi : X' \to X$ is proper and surjective. Moreover, we may arrange it such that there exists a dense open subscheme $U \subset X$ such that $\pi^{-1}(U) \to U$ is an isomorphism."（2925-2928 行）这正是 Noetherian 情形的 Chow's lemma（源 4916-4917 行原文自述："In this section we prove Chow's lemma in the Noetherian case (Lemma \ref{lemma-chow-Noetherian})."）。

实质要求：结论是存在性——必须由本证明造出一个具体对象 $X'$ 连同 $\pi$、浸入 $X' \to \mathbf{P}^n_S$、properness、surjectivity 与在稠密开 $U$ 上的同构这五项同时成立，而不是核对某个更大结果的假设。真正的困难集中在三点：(i) 用一个自造的有限仿射开覆盖 $U_1,\ldots,U_m$（共同含各不可约分支的泛点 $\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_r$）换出「$U = U_1 \cap \ldots \cap U_m$ 稠密且 $U$ 在 $X$ 中概形论稠密」这一可操作前提，并配以 $X \to X^*$ 的归约（2964-2970 行；源 4964-4981 行）；(ii) 把逐分片 $p_i|_{V_i} : V_i \to U_i$ 拼成一个整体态射 $\pi : X' \to X$，并证明它与 $i$ 无关地良定义——依据是「$U \subset X'$ 概形论稠密（由构造），故在开子概型 $V_i \cap V_j$ 中也概形论稠密」，再对 separated 的 $X$ 用 equality-of-morphisms Lemma（3005-3023 行；源 5016-5034 行）；(iii) 反证式地定出 $\pi^{-1}(U_i) = V_i$：proper 像闭 + 概形论稠密夹出等式（3026-3040 行；源 5037-5051 行），由此把 properness 逐片落到 $p_i|_{V_i}$ 上（3042-3048 行；源 5053-5059 行），最后同一招再用一次得 $\pi^{-1}(U) = U$（3050-3060 行；源 5061-5071 行）。

允许引用什么（本 proof 块内全部 $\ref$，共 16 处、16 个不同目标；本 proof 块内不存在任何 \cite，全 dump 该 proof 段内 grep '\cite' 为 0——3063 行前的唯一命中是 2986 行散文 "By the lemma cited above"，不是引用命令）：
- Morphisms, Lemma \ref{morphisms-lemma-finite-type-noetherian}（2935 行）→ 有限型 + Noetherian 底 ⇒ 全程 Noetherian；
- Morphisms, Lemma \ref{morphisms-lemma-permanence-finite-type}、Properties, Lemmas \ref{properties-lemma-locally-Noetherian-quasi-separated}、\ref{properties-lemma-morphism-Noetherian-schemes-quasi-compact}（2938、2940、2941 行）→ 自动 quasi-compact / locally of finite type / quasi-separated；
- Properties, Lemma \ref{properties-lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components}（2945 行）→ 不可约分支有限；
- Properties, Lemma \ref{properties-lemma-point-and-maximal-points-affine}（2952 行）→ 同时含 $x$ 与全部泛点的仿射开；
- Morphisms, Definition \ref{morphisms-definition-scheme-theoretic-image}（2963 行）与 Definition \ref{morphisms-definition-scheme-theoretically-dense}（2970 行）→ 概形论闭包/稠密的定义；
- Morphisms, Lemma \ref{morphisms-lemma-quasi-projective-finite-type-over-S}（2973 行）→ 每个 $U_i$ 的浸入；
- Morphisms, Lemma \ref{morphisms-lemma-quasi-compact-immersion}（2976 行）→ 把浸入补成闭子概型 $Z_i$ 并得概形论稠密开浸入（2986 行 "By the lemma cited above" 即回指此件）；
- Morphisms, Lemma \ref{morphisms-lemma-locally-projective-proper}（2980 行）→ $Z_i \to S$ proper；
- Morphisms, Lemma \ref{morphisms-lemma-factor-factor}（2994-2995 行）→ 交换图表下概形论像之间诱导态射，得 $p_i : Z \to Z_i$；
- Morphisms, Lemma \ref{morphisms-lemma-image-proper-scheme-closed}（2997 与 3037 行，两次）→ $p_i$ proper 与 proper 像闭；
- Constructions, Lemma \ref{constructions-lemma-segre-embedding}（3010 行）→ 积射影空间的 Segre 嵌入；
- Morphisms, Lemma \ref{morphisms-lemma-equality-of-morphisms}（3022 行）→ 概形论稠密 + separated ⇒ 态射相等（粘合良定义）；
- Morphisms, Lemma \ref{morphisms-lemma-proper-local-on-the-base}（3047 行）→ proper 局部于底。
另有陈述部分 2913-2915 行的 \begin{reference}\cite[II Theorem 5.6.1(a)]{EGA}\end{reference}，即该结果的 EGA 出处标注。

必须由本证明完成的具体做法（以上被引件没有一件是该结论本身或其等价形式，全是标准件；EGA 在证明里从未被回指，"cited above" 指的是本节的 morphisms-lemma-quasi-compact-immersion，见源 morphisms.tex:1139 该引理本体）：1) 取有限仿射覆盖 $X = U_1 \cup \ldots \cup U_m$ 使每个 $U_i$ 含 $\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_r$，从而 $U = U_1 \cap \ldots \cap U_m$ 稠密（2944-2959 行；源 4955-4970 行，原文："This and the fact that the $U_i$ are affine opens covering $X$ are all that we will use below."）；2) 以 $X^* = $ 概形论闭包归约到 $U$ 概形论稠密（2961-2970 行；源 4972-4981 行，原文："Hence we may replace $X$ by $X^*$ and $U_i$ by $U_i^*$ and assume that $U$ is scheme theoretically dense in $X$"）；3) 造 $Z_i$、造 $j = (j_1|_U, \ldots, j_m|_U)$、由 "the lemma cited above" 对 $j$ 再取 $Z$ 使 $j : U \to Z$ 是开浸入且 $U$ 在 $Z$ 中概形论稠密（2972-3002 行；源 4983-5013 行）；4) 令 $V_i = p_i^{-1}(U_i)$、$X' = V_1 \cup \ldots \cup V_m$，并由 Segre 嵌入得 $X'$ 到射影空间的浸入（3004-3012 行；源 5015-5023 行）；5) 粘合：这里没有可引的"粘合定理"，本证明自给的机制是「$U$ 在 $X'$ 中概形论稠密 ⇒ 在 $V_i \cap V_j$ 中概形论稠密」＋「$X$ separated」，从而 $p_i|_{V_i \cap V_j} = p_j|_{V_i \cap V_j}$（3014-3023 行；源 5025-5034 行）；6) 用「proper 像闭 + 概形论稠密」夹出 $\pi^{-1}(U_i) = V_i$（3025-3040 行；源 5036-5051 行，原文："Since $V_i \subset \pi^{-1}(U_i)$ is scheme theoretically dense (as it contains $U$) we conclude that $V_i = \pi^{-1}(U_i)$ as claimed."）；7) 由此逐片把 properness 归到 $p_i|_{V_i}$，再经 local-on-base 收口（3042-3048 行；源 5053-5059 行）；8) 同一机制再用一次得 $\pi^{-1}(U) = U$（3050-3060 行；源 5061-5071 行，原文："using that $\text{id}_U : U \to U$ is proper and that $U$ is scheme theoretically dense in $\pi^{-1}(U)$"）。这八步全部是自造对象的构造、自组织归约与自造粘合机制，而不是验证更大结果的假设、按定义检查或拼装已有结果。

结果本身是研究级经典结论（Chow's lemma 的 Noetherian 形式），但据判据，这只决定题目分量、不决定档位；档位由「决定性的一步谁承担」定。

最强反驳（已检查并驳回）：陈述带 \begin{reference}\cite[II Theorem 5.6.1(a)]{EGA}（2913-2915 行），若把该 reference 当作「照抄 EGA 证明」，本条就应压到 H2/H1。驳回理由三条，均可复核：(a) 该 \cite 只出现在 STATEMENT 块内，PROOF 块（2931-3061 行）内无任何 \cite，也从无 "by EGA"、"as in EGA" 之类回指；(b) 全部 16 个 \ref 目标逐一列出如上，全是 Stacks 自身的标准件（定义、分离性、proper 局部性、Segre 嵌入、概形论像），无一给出本结论或其一部分；(c) 结论的五项内容（$X'$ 存在、浸入、proper、surjective、$\pi^{-1}(U) \to U$ 同构）逐项在 3004-3012、3014-3023、3025-3048、3050-3060 行被本证明自己建立，其中 surjectivity 是 $\pi^{-1}(U_i) = V_i$ 且 $U_i$ 覆盖 $X$ 的直接推论。故"决定性的一步被引用"不成立，判 H3。

items.title: Flat-filled increasing binary trees expand products of matroidal hypersimplex classes in the integral matroid Chow ring
items.published_title: Flat-filled increasing binary trees expand products of matroidal hypersimplex classes in the integral matroid Chow ring
items.author: Katz, Eric; Kutler, Max
items.difficulty_reason: The authors derive a local flat-intersection multiplication rule (Lemma 2.6) and construct a weighted bijection between compatible flat insertions and one-vertex binary-tree extensions. Iterating that bijection in a single induction proves a uniform flat-filled increasing binary-tree expansion of an arbitrary product of hypersimplex classes in the integral matroid Chow ring, carrying the exact v-compatibility condition and both the over-intersection and multiplicity weights. This is above the level of applying the degree map or Hodge inequalities: the psi_F flag decomposition of section 2 and the whole compatibility-and-weight apparatus of section 5 must be built first and then combined without losing either weight function.

items.difficulty_reason: The proof develops weak monotonicity of two nonlinear p-Hawking quantities and compares their common asymptotic limit to the volume-capacity mass. It regularizes the p-capacitary equation, passes second-derivative terms distributionally through critical sets, and controls the residual terms by weak Sobolev convergence and dominated convergence. The comparison uses a two-sign asymptotic subsequence argument and combines both monotonic quantities to obtain the precise nonsharp coefficient (5-p)/2.

items.author: Octavio Arizmendi; Adrian Celestino
items.difficulty_reason: The proof lifts the moment character to the decorated Schroder-tree Hopf algebra and analyzes its convolution logarithm. Its new combinatorial step identifies the surviving iterated cuts with strictly order-preserving surjections of the skeleton, producing the Murua coefficients with all multiplicities. Pulling that logarithm through the coalgebra morphism gives the multivariate formula without a multiplicative Mobius inversion, which is unavailable for monotone cumulants.

题面（b9-dump.txt:626-636；源 dga.tex statement_lines=[7070, 7079]，label=lemma-countable，env=lemma），逐字（dump:629-635）：
「Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra with
$H^i(A)$ countable for each $i$. Let $M$ be an object of $D(A, \text{d})$.
Then the following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $M = \text{hocolim} E_n$ with $E_n$ compact in $D(A, \text{d})$, and
\item $H^i(M)$ is countable for each $i$.
\end{enumerate}」
即：设微分分次代数 $(A, \text{d})$ 的各阶上同调 $H^i(A)$ 可数，则 $D(A, \text{d})$ 的对象 $M$ 是「compact 对象的 homotopy colimit」当且仅当各阶 $H^i(M)$ 可数。题面本身不假设 $A$ 可数，也不假设 $M$ 可被可数模表示——这两点只能在证明内造出来。

实质要求：等价的两向都要证。(1)$\Rightarrow$(2)（dump:639-649）要把「homotopy colimit 的上同调是各层上同调的余极限」与「compact 对象的结构」拼起来，把可数性从各层传到 $M$。(2)$\Rightarrow$(1)（dump:650-755）是本条重心，作者自陈「The interesting implication is the other one.」（dump:650）：在不假设 $A$、$M$ 可数的前提下，先造出与 $A$ 上同调同构的可数微分分次子代数 $A'$ 并把问题降到 $A'$，再降到「$A$ 可数、$M$ 是可数微分分次模」，取可数的 (P)-消解，把该消解写成有限滤过的（因而是 compact 的）微分分次子模的可数上升并，最后用 homotopy colimit 收口。故本条既含自造对象（$A_n$、$A'$、$P'_n$）与极限/并的论证，也含两处外推。

items.author: Dave Witte Morris
items.difficulty_reason: The proof strengthens geometric generation to a uniformly bounded number of rank-one factors while retaining polynomial norm control. 题面（b7-dump.txt:1670-1682；源 flat.tex statement_lines=[12485,12496]，label=lemma-trivial-fibres-dvr，env=lemma）：“Let $f : X \to S$ be a proper morphism with geometrically connected fibres where $S$ is the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring. Denote $\eta \in S$ the generic point and denote $X_n \subset X$ the closed subscheme cutout by the $n$th power of a uniformizer on $S$. Then there exists an integer $n$ such that the following is true: any finite locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{E}$ such that $\mathcal{E}|_{X_\eta}$ and $\mathcal{E}|_{X_n}$ are free, is free.”（逐字照抄，仅将原文换行接为一行）

实质要求：这是带定量的存在性断言——要造出一个只依赖 $X$（不依赖 $\mathcal{E}$）的整数 $n$，并证明“在一般纤维与第 $n$ 个无穷小邻域上都自由 $\Rightarrow$ 整体自由”。难点在于自由性只给在开纤维与 $\pi$-幂零邻域这两端，中间全部 $\pi$-挠信息必须被单个有限的 $n$ 一次性压住；这既不是按定义核对，也不是把某个现成定理的假设逐条验证。

允许引用的输入（全文恰引八条，均为通用工具，无一条以本题结论或等价命题为内容）：Krull–Akizuki（Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-integral-closure-Dedekind}，1688-1689）造 DVR 扩张 $A \subset B$；proper 的赋值判别法（Morphisms, Lemma \ref{morphisms-lemma-characterize-proper}，1692-1693）得 $B$-值点与截面；平坦基变换（Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma \ref{coherent-lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology}，1698-1700）；Varieties, Lemma \ref{varieties-lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections}（1719-1720，原文仅作 hint）；Artin–Rees（Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma \ref{coherent-lemma-Artin-Rees}，1749-1751）用于选 $k$；More on Algebra, Example \ref{more-algebra-example-finite-injective-finite-global-dimension}（1783-1784）DVR 上复形分裂为 $\bigoplus H^i[-i]$；Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma \ref{coherent-lemma-proper-over-affine-cohomology-finite}（1787-1788）上同调为有限 $A$-模；More on Algebra, Lemma \ref{more-algebra-lemma-generalized-valuation-ring-modules}（1789-1791）DVR 上有限模分解为循环模直和。

必须由本证明完成的部分（逐条对应原文定位）：
(a) 自组织归约到有截面（1685-1721）：取 $X_\eta$ 的闭点 $\xi$，由 Krull–Akizuki 造 $A \subset B$ 使 $\mathrm{Frac}(B) = \kappa(\xi)$，用赋值判别法得 $\tau : \Spec(B) \to X$ 并诱导截面 $\sigma : \Spec(B) \to X_B$；再由平坦基变换断言 $H^0(X_B, \mathcal{E}_B) = H^0(X, \mathcal{E}) \otimes_A B$，取出 $r$ 个整体截面 $s_1, \ldots, s_r$ 生成 $\tau^*\mathcal{E}$（1701-1705），取行列式得函数 $g$，在“the fibres are proper and connected”下断定“$g$ must be invertible”（1715-1720）——此处原文自承“(details omitted; hint: use Varieties, Lemma …)”，是本题唯一被省略的细节，但它只服务归约，不是结论机制。
(b) 核心构造之一：模 $\pi^k$ 的复形替换（1724-1775）。设已有截面后，把 $\mathcal{E}$ 的自由性等价于 $H^0(K) = H^0(X, \mathcal{E}) \to A^{\oplus r}$ 满（$K = R\Gamma(X, \mathcal{E})$，1733-1734，原文“Arguing as above”）；置 $L = R\Gamma(X, \mathcal{O}_X^{\oplus r})$ 为已满足该满性的参照物（1737-1738），由一般纤维自由得 $K \otimes_A Q(A) \cong L \otimes_A Q(A)$（1739-1741）。关键一步全在本证明内：先认出 $K \otimes_A^{\mathbf L} A/\pi^m A = R\Gamma(X, \mathcal{E} \xrightarrow{\pi^m} \mathcal{E})$（1741-1746），用 Artin–Rees 选 $k > 0$ 使 $(\mathcal{O}_X)_{tors} \to \mathcal{O}_X/\pi^k \mathcal{O}_X$ 单（1749-1751），再由“$\mathcal{E}$ 在 $X_n$ 上自由”把 $\mathcal{E}$ 的 $\pi^m$-复形在模 $\pi^k$ 意义下换成 $\mathcal{O}_X^{\oplus r}$ 的 $\pi^m$-复形：对 $n \geq m + k$ 有 $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ 中的同构链 $(\mathcal{E} \xrightarrow{\pi^m} \mathcal{E}) \cong (\mathcal{E}/\pi^k\mathcal{E} \xrightarrow{\pi^m} \mathcal{E}/\pi^{k + m}\mathcal{E}) \cong (\mathcal{O}_X^{\oplus r}/\pi^k\mathcal{O}_X^{\oplus r} \xrightarrow{\pi^m} \mathcal{O}_X^{\oplus r}/\pi^{k + m}\mathcal{O}_X^{\oplus r}) \cong (\mathcal{O}_X^{\oplus r} \xrightarrow{\pi^m} \mathcal{O}_X^{\oplus r})$（1754-1765），从而得 $K \otimes_A^{\mathbf L} A/\pi^m A \cong L \otimes_A^{\mathbf L} A/\pi^m A$（1766-1770），且与 $\sigma$ 的拉回相容，故 $K \otimes_A^{\mathbf L} A/\pi^m A \to (A/\pi^m A)^{\oplus r}$ 在 $0$ 次上满（1771-1775）。这一层“把自由性假设搬进导出范畴并截断”没有任何被引件代劳。

据此，$n$ 的存在性、$n$ 的取值构造，以及全部机制（Artin–Rees 定 $k$、模 $\pi^k$ 复形替换、$e$ 定界、在 $\pi^{e+1}$ 层上反推 $H^0$ 满）都由本证明承担；被引八条只提供基变换、有限性、DVR 模结构、赋值判别等通用工具，无一条以本题结论或等价命题为内容。本题亦非双射/等价型断言，故“两个方向的机制”条款不触发（证明内部用到的“$\mathcal{E}$ 自由 $\iff$ $H^0(K) \to A^{\oplus r}$ 满”是自证的，见 1733-1734）。

items.author: Lisa Carbone; Alex J. Feingold; Walter Freyn
items.difficulty_reason: The proof builds a geometric chamber model in the Lorentzian Cartan slice and glues its compact-real-form translates by parabolic face stabilizers. It uses explicit simple-root SU(2) Cartan rotations to relate wall geometry to the building panels, then proves well-definedness, injectivity, surjectivity and both Weyl-valued distance compatibilities. The target is the semisimple adjoint-orbit model at fixed negative norm, not all elements of the infinite-dimensional Lie algebra.

items.difficulty_reason: The new obstacle is that distinct admissible colors can share Dehn-twist eigenvalues at a composite level, so the prime-level irreducibility argument does not transfer directly. The author establishes vacuum cyclicity through tensor Vandermonde separation and bounds the commutant using two banded-graph bases. An explicit genus-one swapping operator lifts to commuting handle operators whose squared action rules out the remaining nonscalar commutant direction.

items.title: For a complex semisimple g and nonroot-of-unity q, a tensor product of two irreducible highest-weight U_q(g)-modules with an infinite-dimensional factor is completely reducible exactly when the product contravariant form is nondegenerate on its singular vectors
items.published_title: For a complex semisimple g and nonroot-of-unity q, a tensor product of two irreducible highest-weight U_q(g)-modules with an infinite-dimensional factor is completely reducible exactly when the product contravariant form is nondegenerate on its singular vectors
items.author: Andrey I. Mudrov
items.difficulty_reason: The difficult direction must show that nondegeneracy on singular vectors exhausts the entire possibly infinite-dimensional tensor product, not merely that its visible highest-weight submodules split. The author constructs reciprocal extremal spaces and a twist operator, identifies its form with the tensor Shapovalov restriction, and proves both exhaustion and irreducibility by height induction. This addresses a genuine infinite-dimensional representation-theory problem beyond the finite-dimensional Weyl theorem.

items.title: Finitely presented schemes, morphisms and equality descend through inverse systems of quasi-compact quasi-separated bases with affine transition maps
items.published_title: Finitely presented schemes, morphisms and equality descend through inverse systems of quasi-compact quasi-separated bases with affine transition maps
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: This categorical finite-presentation descent theorem must descend entire scheme objects, all morphisms and equality relations across arbitrary affine-transition inverse systems. Its proof constructs finite affine models, synchronizes overlap opens and isomorphisms at successive indices, and enforces the cocycle before gluing, without a Noetherian or separatedness assumption. The global categorical coherence construction is beyond routine ring coefficient descent.

items.difficulty_reason: The difficult step is to bound formal exponents at irregular singularities from the raw Laurent coefficients, which need not equal the residue eigenvalues. items.title: For Riemannian Painleve metrics with genuine variable blocks, the generalized Robertson conditions are equivalent to vanishing of every off-block-diagonal Ricci component
items.published_title: For Riemannian Painleve metrics with genuine variable blocks, the generalized Robertson conditions are equivalent to vanishing of every off-block-diagonal Ricci component
items.author: Thierry Daude; Niky Kamran; Francois Nicoleau
items.difficulty_reason: The Staeckel one-variable identity does not control the additional curvature terms caused by blocks of dimension greater than one. The author calculates all cross-block Christoffel contractions and shows that their dependence on the arbitrary intrinsic block metrics cancels. Generalized Levi-Civita identities then remove the new remainder terms, giving the geometric Ricci characterization of grouped separation conditions.

items.author: Alexey Slinkin; Alexander Varchenko
items.difficulty_reason: Compatibility of the de Rham differential with the current-algebra action requires nontrivial affine-Verma identities at every pole order, not just agreement on logarithmic one-forms. The authors prove those identities by evaluating all PBW basis types and controlling higher-current commutator cancellations, then use them in both the finite-point and infinity expansions of the chain map. The injection remains valid at resonant highest weights, while the noncritical level and shifted degrees are essential.

items.title: Every quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space over the integers is an affine-transition inverse limit of finite-type quasi-separated integer algebraic spaces
items.published_title: Every quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space over the integers is an affine-transition inverse limit of finite-type quasi-separated integer algebraic spaces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem builds finite-type integer models of an arbitrary qcqs algebraic space through finite Nisnevich filtration, relative scheme approximation and explicit gluing of finite-stage etale equivalence relations. The new relation is manufactured by adjoining the complement diagonal to a descended overlap relation, then cartesian transitions and quotient limits are recovered. This non-schematic approximation/effectiveness construction is substantially beyond routine scheme descent or formal parameter changes.

items.title: For Noetherian local algebras over characteristic-p fields, geometric regularity is equivalent to regularity and canonical cotangent or absolute-differential injectivity
items.published_title: For Noetherian local algebras over characteristic-p fields, geometric regularity is equivalent to regularity and canonical cotangent or absolute-differential injectivity
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The author characterizes geometric regularity of an arbitrary Noetherian local algebra over an imperfect characteristic-p field through cotangent H1 and absolute differential injectivity. Its hard direction uses independent p-root field extensions, explicit zero-differential cotangent presentations, Cartier dimension equalities and two coupled conormal diagrams to recover differential independence; the opposite direction controls embedding dimension under every finite purely inseparable extension. These inseparability/cotangent dimension arguments are substantially beyond ordinary Jacobian checks.

items.difficulty_reason: Ordinary Kunneth does not identify the irregular Hodge filtration after adding the two exponential potentials, because the product compactification can develop indeterminacy. items.title: Birkhoff face lattices force standard symmetric-group representation polytopes
items.published_title: Birkhoff face lattices force standard symmetric-group representation polytopes
items.author: Baumeister, Barbara; Ladisch, Frieder
items.difficulty_reason: The proof reconstructs the full combinatorial symmetry group from intersection counts of complements of Birkhoff facets, then transports commuting regular actions into that group. A Chermak–Delgado measure and normalizer argument constrains the group, while a stabilizer facet, Frobenius reciprocity, and a representation-polytope dimension formula isolate the standard constituent. The explicit C6 case at n=3 handles the low-dimensional exception; combining polytope face combinatorics, finite-group structure, and character theory exceeds routine doctoral qualifying material.

items.title: Cyclic ordered-partition free resolution of digraph lattice ideals
items.published_title: Cyclic ordered-partition free resolution of digraph lattice ideals
items.author: O'Carroll, Liam; Planas-Vilanova, Francesc
items.difficulty_reason: The construction assigns generators of the Cyc complex from cyclically ordered vertex partitions and ties differential coefficients to distance data from the adjugate Laplacian; showing it is a complex and exact in degree zero does not establish the full resolution. The inductive step identifies selected Schreyer tau-syzygies from weighted reverse-lexicographic Groebner bases with each next differential, using partition correspondences and monomial-quotient generators across homological degrees. This combines directed-graph Laplacians, lattice ideals, Groebner basis theory, and homological algebra in a uniform all-n resolution argument beyond doctoral qualifying material.

For the stability part the solver must set up the sharp-energy variational problem, recognise that a failure of orbital stability produces a sequence of initial data whose energy converges to the maximization value with impulse and $L^p$-norm bounded by $\mu$ and $\sigma$, keep that property along the flow through the Yudovich conservation law, and then extract from Theorem 5.2 a maximizer that contradicts the assumed separation from the maximizer set; the $p=\infty$ case additionally requires the decomposition of the data into a maximizer and a remainder, the comparison of the two energies through the sharp energy inequality, and the recovery of the impulse of the remainder from the convergence of the impulse of the maximizer part. It must differentiate the Monge--Amp\`ere equation along the flat direction to obtain the linearised equation for $u_{11}$, form the quantity $\Phi=\log u_{11}+\log|u|+\frac12u_1^2$, and then split the maximum of $\Phi$ over the section into the interior case, where the concavity of the log-determinant and the structural conditions force the second-order test to fail, and the boundary case, where the boundary equation, the tangential derivatives, the log-concavity of the target density with its Euler identity, and finally a shearing transformation preserving the flat direction are needed to reduce the boundary point to the interior case. items.published_title: All intrinsic characteristic classes of a smooth Lie algebroid pull back functorially along every transverse smooth map, without a connectivity condition on its fibers
items.author: Pedro Frejlich
items.difficulty_reason: The adjoint representation up to homotopy of an inverse-image Lie algebroid is not just the pullback adjoint bundle. The proof constructs a compatible connection that splits off the doubled vertical bundle with matching metric connections and identifies the resulting graded Chern-Simons forms. Transverse normal forms and graph factorization then extend the exact identity from submersions to arbitrary transverse maps.

It bounds the expected number of cycles of an arbitrary random cycle-factor of a directed d-regular graph on n vertices by 2(n/d)(log d + 1) + (n/d) log_2(d!) - H(C), which is the technical core of the article and the input to its main theorems. The proof is complete inside the retained span: it represents the cycle-factor as a random permutation, applies the chain rule for entropy along a uniformly random vertex order, identifies the entropy loss compared with a uniform permutation, shows that the number of available out-neighbours is uniform on [d], converts the probability that a step closes a cycle into 2 over the number of available out-neighbours plus the entropy loss, and sums the resulting harmonic series. It is not a routine exercise: it is Radhakrishnan's proof of the Bregman-Minc inequality reworked with an explicit bookkeeping of the total entropy loss, and the article presents that bookkeeping as its new contribution. Required context: the article's own Lemma 3.3 on the probability of an atom of a random variable in terms of the entropy loss, retained in statement form. Rated H2 rather than H3 because the argument, although clever and research level, is a single entropy calculation built on a classical template that the article itself names.

items.author: Filomena De Filippis, Antonella Nastasi, Cintia Pacchiano Camacho
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem 3.1 (source0.tex lines 788--797), the Euler-Lagrange system satisfied by a constrained local minimizer of the double phase functional with target as in condition (a), delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 798--847 (50 lines, one adjacent proof environment, no gap and no deferral). The proof is not a routine verification: for a general target set the minimisation property cannot be linearised by a convexity argument, and the article says so explicitly. The author argument covers the boundary of the target with finitely many balls, builds a partition of unity and a local frame of vector fields tangent to the boundary, decomposes an arbitrary test field into its tangential and normal parts, and then varies the minimiser in two different ways: along the flow of a tangential field, which produces the identity that becomes the left-hand side of the system, and along the normal field v, which produces a Radon measure lambda through the Riesz representation theorem and then, after proving that lambda does not depend on the cut-off parameter, a density function theta through the Radon-Nikodym theorem. Both variations are combined with the partition of unity and the identity d/ddelta of the functional at delta = 0 to yield the stated system. The substantive steps are the construction of the test fields, the identification of the limit of the two boundary integrals as the cut-off parameter vanishes using the tangential identity for the distance function, and the passage from the Radon measure to its boundary density; none of them is an unpacking of definitions. H2: a complete original research-paper theorem, moderately short, whose proof is a genuinely technical variational argument rather than a routine exercise.

items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the article's Theorem 5 (source label 'th:1'): for a true system in Sigma_cont, Sigma_cont-informativity of the data for stabilization is equivalent to plain informativity for stabilization, and any gain that stabilizes every data-consistent controllable system stabilizes every data-consistent system. The unit is above ordinary PhD qualifying level because the counted proof is not a citation and cannot be reached by textbook linear algebra alone: the authors perturb the true system along the data-consistency directions through the set of (A_0,B_0) with A_0 X_- + B_0 U_- = 0, and the argument then rests on two auxiliary results whose complete proofs are retained inside the unit. The first, Lemma 7, shows that a controllable pair stays controllable along the whole affine line except for at most n^2 parameter values, by exhibiting a square submatrix of the Kalman controllability matrix that is nonsingular at the controllable point and whose determinant is a polynomial of degree at most n^2. The second, Lemma 9, shows that if a matrix pencil M + delta N is Schur on a half-line minus finitely many points then N is nilpotent and the pencil is Schur on the whole real line, by observing that the traces of all powers are bounded polynomials on that half-line, hence constant, and then invoking Horn and Johnson's characterization of equality of spectra through traces of powers. Combining data informativity with a polynomial perturbation argument and deducing a stability conclusion for one uncontrollable data-consistent system from a hypothesis on all controllable data-consistent systems, and thereby showing that controllability as prior knowledge does not relax the stabilization conditions, is research-level data-driven control theory rather than a qualifying-examination exercise.

items.difficulty_reason: The elliptic part removes a flat nonlinear error by proving periodicity through injective first-integral maps on shrinking transverse balls and propagating that property across singular levels. A blow-up then makes the period correction smooth and flat, allowing circle-action linearization and a further invariant multiplier normalization. This new smooth mechanism exceeds applying a formal normal-form theorem or the hyperbolic Sternberg-Chen theorem.

items.title: Uniqueness of the minimizer of the balanced optimal-transport assignment step from a balanced partition initialization
items.published_title: Uniqueness of the minimizer of the balanced optimal-transport assignment step from a balanced partition initialization
items.author: Wenyan Luo, Dustin G. Mixon
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the article's Theorem 14 (source label 'thm.generic initialization by partition'): if the data points are generic and the initial centroids are the centroids of a balanced partition of those points, then the minimizer of the balanced optimal-transport cost over the assignment polytope is unique. The unit is above ordinary PhD qualifying level because the counted proof is a complete seventy-line research argument rather than a routine uniqueness check: it passes to distinct integral vertices of the optimal face of the assignment polytope, encodes each vertex by a set-valued assignment map of the data into the classes of the partition, shows that equality of the two costs forces a polynomial identity in the data points and hence, by genericity, an exact term-by-term cancellation, extracts from that cancellation the exchange property relating the two assignment maps on their disagreement set, and then propagates the exchange property class by class until it exhibits a strict cost decrease, contradicting optimality. Combining the geometry of the assignment polytope, genericity of the data and a combinatorial propagation of an exchange relation is research-level work in the theory of balanced clustering and optimal transport, well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations.

items.difficulty_reason: Equivariant cyclic covers define the filtered rational-power D-module. The twisted logarithmic Spencer complex is proved exact by explicit local normal-form induction; toric normalization then determines the round-up lattice and eigenspace filtration. Strictness yields the birational vanishing and exact filtered image computing every Hodge ideal only after those complete new constructions.

The author uses etale projective reduction, universal injectivity on residue fibres, an annihilator-radical argument for the base condition, and auto-associated local-ring projective criteria for the converse. This is the full structural tensor formula, rather than a local auxiliary or an openness consequence.

items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the article's Proposition 3.1 (source label 'nse'), the viscous counterpart of the paper's self-similarity analysis: if a solution of the 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes equation splits into a regular part whose L^4(dt;L^2) norm is finite and an inner part supported in a ball of radius of order (1-t)^gamma whose L^2 norm is bounded by C(1-t)^{-1+3gamma/2}, then any blow up at time one forces gamma at most one half. The unit is above ordinary PhD qualifying level because the counted proof is a complete argument that combines the two hypotheses rather than invoking a black box: it adds the inner and outer contributions to the L^4 norm of the vorticity, uses the explicit growth of the inner profile and the integrability of the outer part to bound the time integral by Gamma plus an explicit constant divided by 6 gamma minus 3, and then concludes that if gamma exceeds one half that integral is finite, which contradicts blow up by the classical regularity criterion. The bookkeeping of the exponent and the exact dependence on gamma is the point of the result, and it is research-level analysis of the Navier-Stokes equations rather than a qualifying-examination exercise.

items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the article's Lemma 14 (source label 'lemmaNonAm'): in the Cayley graph of the fundamental group of the manifold, for every radius R > 2 the ratio of the number of vertices in the sphere of radius R to the number of vertices in the ball of radius R-1 is at most twice the vertex degree minus one. The unit is above ordinary PhD qualifying level because the counted proof is a complete covering argument rather than a counting exercise: it fixes an arbitrary vertex in the annulus between the two balls, exhibits a neighbour in the smaller ball (an ancestor obtained from the fundamental domain adjacent to the vertex), deduces from that construction that at most degree-minus-one edges leave the smaller ball for the sphere, and combines the resulting edge count with the degree bound to produce exactly the stated ratio. The lemma is the quantitative input of the paper's estimate of the expected weight of an essential vertex, and the argument mixes the geometry of the fundamental domain with the combinatorics of the Cayley graph, which is research-level geometric group theory rather than a qualifying-examination exercise.

items.published_title: Principality of algebraic equivariant fusion for Hopf algebras with bijective antipode, principal comodule algebras and two jointly surjective C-star quotient maps
items.author: Ludwik Dabrowski; Tom Hadfield; Piotr M. Hajac
items.difficulty_reason: The construction combines the original strong connection with an antipode-controlled trivial connection through two square-root cutoff elements obtained by C-star functional calculus. The proof verifies both quotient boundary constraints and the canonical splitting, then derives Hopf-Galois bijectivity and equivariant projectivity from a nonunital connection criterion; it covers fusion without a pullback join decomposition.

items.author: Paul F. Baum; Piotr M. Hajac
items.difficulty_reason: The proof reduces an arbitrary compact group to finite-dimensional associated unitary-group bundles, then glues algebraic canonical-map preimages from local trivializations using square-root partitions of unity. It establishes an algebraic bijectivity criterion without assuming a Lie group, manifold base or local triviality for the original action, combining topological freeness with finite-isotypic Hopf-algebra structure.

items.difficulty_reason: Standard Day convolution, Gabriel localisation and pure-injective representability do not by themselves identify the maximal localising tensor ideals needed for this support. The author establishes the unique maximal localising tensor ideal extending a given maximal Serre ideal, using the internal-Hom kernel of its pure-injective residue weak ring and injective-hull comparisons across quotients. This nonroutine correspondence supplies the vanishing dichotomy that proves the tensor-product formula for arbitrary noncompact objects.

items.difficulty_reason: Classical analytic smoothing and a KAM step do not alone preserve frequency-Lipschitz invariant graphs at the stated finite differentiability threshold. The author adapts the weighted truncation and iteration to control the simultaneous small-divisor and composition losses, and derives sharper difference estimates for the graph maps than for the conjugacies. The convergence argument then proves the stated graph regularity and uniform frequency-Lipschitz bounds without assuming such bounds for the dynamics.

items.difficulty_reason: The definitions of parahoric cuspidal functions and Levi induction do not alone identify this orbital-distribution pairing or its exact volume factors. items.difficulty_reason: The cited compact action-set factor theorem and Kneser critical-pair theorem do not alone identify the original action's full transfer-time set or its endpoints. The author establishes a measurable transfer-time correspondence with a quantitative overshoot inequality and uses equality of the densities to recover the actual circle factor and sets. items.difficulty_reason: The classical Jacobi semigroup and Bernstein-function prerequisites do not themselves construct the nonlocal generator with the stated positive invariant density. The author proves the necessary moment factorisation and full support, builds an explicit polynomial intertwining and maximum-principle/resolvent argument, and transfers the invariant measure without assuming the resulting Markov process exists. Those constructions then establish the polynomial core, invariant-law uniqueness and ergodicity in the genuinely nonzero jump-kernel case.

items.published_title: Detecting open orbits of faithful connected solvable actions with nontrivial unipotents by bounded generalized root subgroups in characteristic zero
items.author: Andriy Regeta; Immanuel van Santen
items.difficulty_reason: The cited rational quotient and solvable invariant-fraction results do not by themselves produce root subgroups of a prescribed common weight and arbitrarily large dimension. The author combines two equal-weight semi-invariants with a homogeneous additive action to construct the displayed replicated actions, and verifies faithfulness through the independence of their homogeneous powers. That same-weight replication construction supplies the unbounded family needed for the converse implication, together with the exact vector-field/root-subgroup comparison.

items.difficulty_reason: A fixed-inradius constraint prevents the usual unconstrained Blaschke deformation argument from identifying the area minimiser directly. The author proves rigidity of the admissible clusters, derives their exact area formula and strict interior concavity, and uses the constrained arc-count optimisation to exclude competing polygon configurations. This geometric reduction and analytic sign construction establish the unique polygon optimiser without relying on the separate density claim for arbitrary constant-width bodies.

items.title: Arbitrarily large separation of uniform viscous observation time from flushing time on smooth bounded connected Euclidean domains
items.published_title: Arbitrarily large separation of uniform viscous observation time from flushing time on smooth bounded connected Euclidean domains
items.author: Camille Laurent; Matthieu Léautaud
items.difficulty_reason: The geometric flushing condition does not itself control the small-viscosity observability time. The author constructs a smooth family with a fixed positive bottom energy, combines the weighted eigenfunction/quasimode estimates with its observation geometry, and proves a uniformly bounded exit time for the corresponding trajectories. The same family then has a growing observation lower bound, so the separation requires both the spectral construction and the explicit dynamical argument.

items.difficulty_reason: The cited Franks standardisation and Bismut--Zhang theorem do not by themselves compare the dynamical Milnor metric with the analytic metric for the original Morse--Smale flow. The author constructs the untwisted determinant-line fusion comparison through orbit destruction and proves the matching variation of the characteristic current. Tracking those metric and current contributions, including the negative-vector-field sign, is the nonroutine step that makes the final comparison formula hold.

items.difficulty_reason: The residue theorem only gives the sum-zero constraint and does not characterize the exceptional integral resonances for a single zero. The authors construct and recognize weighted connection trees by gluing flat polar domains, then prove commensurability of every excluded configuration and the sharp integer total bound through leaf-removal induction. The reverse saddle-connection-length argument supplies the full obstruction rather than merely a sufficient gluing recipe.

items.difficulty_reason: The author constructs a global transitive Lie algebroid by gluing infinitesimal homogeneous actions, then reverses the construction through source-simply-connected integration and an equivariant developing map. items.difficulty_reason: The centerline Stokeslet formula and minimum-dissipation principle do not give uniform errors as filament capacity degenerates. The authors prove the boundary and near-centerline asymptotics, construct divergence-free extensions with constants uniform in filament thickness, and build a capacitary test field for the local Sobolev error. These estimates produce the stated different logarithmic rates rather than a direct formal rescaling of a fixed-domain bound.

items.author: Camilla Felisetti; Mirko Mauri
items.difficulty_reason: The named Simpson properness theorem does not itself construct a projective compactification of the whole Hodge family. Section3 builds the parameter-compatible equivariant quotient, identifies its open Hodge moduli locus and controls the descended line bundle on the zero fiber by the compactified Hitchin map. The boundary twist and comparison with the trivial nonzero-parameter family then close relative ampleness; these source-specific constructions remain required after the cited GIT and ampleness foundations are allowed.

items.difficulty_reason: Orbit equivalence of each vertex action does not directly produce a free action of the graph product on a common probability space. Section4 transplants the measurable vertex orbit cocycle through a graph-product retraction and checks that its variable labels preserve commutation along links. items.author: Nicolas Curien; Igor Kortchemski; Cyril Marzouk
items.difficulty_reason: A pointwise enumeration ratio is insufficient to determine the defect law because mass could escape through arbitrarily large defects. Sections2–3 prove the exact core-kernel enumeration and uniform near-trivalent contraction ratios, transferring loop controls through Catalan-weighted forests. Section4 combines those new estimates with a uniform factorial tail to normalize the finite-crossover Poisson law, so its difficulty is not the final ratio-to-Poisson calculation alone.

items.published_title: Simultaneous exact finite-dimensional and approximate all-direction shape desensitization of the heat equation for disjoint control and observation sets with connected observation complement
items.author: Sylvain Ervedoza; Pierre Lissy; Yannick Privat
items.difficulty_reason: Dense linear Neumann traces alone cannot solve the quadratic shape-response constraints while keeping all remaining directions small. Section2 constructs paired time-separated trace targets so that the finite-dimensional quadratic response can be controlled, then closes the exact constraints through a Brouwer correction. The final approximate-control stage must preserve that nonlinear correction uniformly, which remains a substantive construction after standard heat and fixed-point foundations are allowed.

items.title: A perfect generator detects bounded-above quasi-coherent derived objects on every quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme through eventual Ext vanishing
items.published_title: A perfect generator detects bounded-above quasi-coherent derived objects on every quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme through eventual Ext vanishing
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: A single assumed generator detects eventual cohomological boundedness of an arbitrary unbounded quasi-coherent derived object, without an ample line bundle or Noetherian hypothesis. The proof spreads eventual vanishing to all perfect probes via finite thick generation, then uses closed-support Koszul truncation detection and a lifted local generator in a finite-affine induction to force global boundedness. This compatibility of the derived boundedness structure with a global generator is stronger than mere nonzero-object detection.

items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the article's Theorem 4.1 (source label 'thm:floor'), the indistinguishability floor of the paper's structural identifiability analysis: for a target entity whose stabiliser acts on the orbit of the true owner, every structural scoring rule is constant along that orbit, so ranking the true owner against a uniformly random orbit member has expected ROC-AUC exactly one half and the probability that the true owner is ranked strictly first is at most the reciprocal of the orbit size. The unit is above ordinary PhD qualifying level because the counted proof is not a numerical computation but a symmetry argument about identifiability: it transports an arbitrary pair of orbit members by a stabiliser element that fixes the target, applies isomorphism invariance of the scoring rule to show that the score is constant on the orbit, and then converts that constancy into the two quantitative evaluation consequences, namely the exact chance-level AUC and the tie-based bound on the top-one probability. Deriving an information-theoretic impossibility statement from group-theoretic invariance and drawing the evaluation consequences for a deployed scoring pipeline is research-level work in structural identifiability, beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations.

items.difficulty_reason: The author constructs a global representation intertwiner by Fourier coefficients along a rational codimension-one abelian subgroup, and organizes its infinite-dimensional induced summands through lattice coadjoint orbits. The proof establishes the rational subgroup needed for an arbitrary lattice, proves the Parseval isometry, and constructs an explicit periodized inverse on a dense subspace. This combines nilpotent orbit theory with lattice and Hilbert-space reconstruction beyond ordinary qualifying-exam Fourier or representation arguments.

items.author: Marie-Claude Arnaud; Jacques Fejoz
items.difficulty_reason: Transverse volume growth alone does not give an entropy bound when images of a transversal can return through many plaques. The authors construct a uniform leafwise-distance comparison and a finite product-chart partition, then prove that each dynamical itinerary intersects every terminal plaque at most once. This new geometric control gives a uniform volume bound per itinerary and forces exponentially many itineraries, rather than relying on the smoother Yomdin volume-growth theorem.

items.published_title: Every non-neat nonconstant periodic orbit of a smooth Hamiltonian with positive definite fiber Hessian is a round trip
items.author: Patrick Bernard
items.difficulty_reason: Local uniqueness of Hamiltonian trajectories does not classify all returns of their projections to the base, and a non-neat orbit can contain both degenerate and self-intersection times. The author rules out transverse self-intersections globally, uses the energy-preserving fiber symmetry to construct a decreasing involution on every nondegenerate interval, and closes the time circle at the two turning points. The square-root coordinate then gives smoothness through the turning points, providing the new global round-trip classification beyond the ordinary local implicit-function theorem.

items.difficulty_reason: A homeomorphism can align branch points adaptively, so mismatch at one random branch or a fixed map does not give a simultaneous obstruction for all homeomorphisms. The authors control exponentially many admissible branch-point chains and use a corrected positive-martingale mismatch argument to force uniform loss of region mass across recursive scales. Only after that new probabilistic core do Brownian excursion regularity and region-diameter bounds convert the mass loss into the strict Holder obstruction.

items.title: Countable bubble decomposition with conservation of bubbling mass for bounded positive measures
items.published_title: Countable bubble decomposition with conservation of bubbling mass for bounded positive measures
items.author: Antonin Monteil; Paul Pegon
items.difficulty_reason: Banach-Alaoglu compactness and Portmanteau inequalities only yield local vague limits and allow mass to escape; they do not provide one subsequence with countably many simultaneously separated profiles. The authors construct nested extractions, a diagonal family of expanding balls and quantitative mass errors, then control every translated limit of the remainder by a decreasing bubbling quantity. They finally recenter each bubble in the support of the original measure while preserving narrow convergence and the whole bubbling-mass sum, which is nonroutine beyond qualifying-examination measure compactness.

The authors control extension obstructions, compute the class/Picard and intersection scaling, and prove global generation and cohomology constancy for the relevant divisorial sheaves. items.difficulty_reason: The argument constructs a strict affinoid neighborhood and a regular curve model whose specialization fiber simultaneously preserves the analytic neighborhood and realizes its bounded-function ring as a complete two-dimensional regular local ring. Its new local core then descends rational points through two successive discrete valuation rings and applies Hensel lifting, using the precise compatibility of their valuations with the ground field. Standard properness and Hensel lemmas alone do not supply that analytic-to-local-algebra construction; the full authored construction and nested auxiliary proofs are preserved and exceed ordinary PhD qualification exercises.

items.author: David Fisher; Mahan Mj; Wouter van Limbeek
items.difficulty_reason: The usual finite-index-subgroup counting argument fails when the infinite normal subgroup is not finitely generated. The authors use the locally finite Cayley-Abels graph to construct a finite-index subgroup as a finite-ball stabilizer and prove that its fibers are invariant under the whole lattice. This new normalization construction then lets discrete normalizers force the two ambient lattices to be commensurable, beyond the classical rigidity and normalizer prerequisites alone.

items.author: Frédéric Lagoutière; Filippo Santambrogio; Sébastien Tran Tien
items.difficulty_reason: Weak compactness alone does not identify the nonlinear interaction force when mass concentrates at atoms and the Lipschitz potential has a nondifferentiable diagonal. The authors symmetrize that interaction, pass both dissipative terms through the viscosity limit and use equality in the limiting energy inequality to recover the exact velocity field with zero diagonal convention. This new nonlinear measure-level identification closes the aggregation equation, beyond the standard Wasserstein compactness or gradient-flow foundations.

items.difficulty_reason: The cited orthogonal-connection criterion alone does not produce a connection on the chosen nonsplit tensor product: the authors exclude every positive-degree isotropic decomposition, using stability and a splitting contradiction for the rank-two case. They then identify its stable rank-two destabilizer and show that connection invariance of its perpendicular would force a forbidden degree-zero connection. The new quasi-filtration obstruction and odd-rank filtration equivalence transfer that obstruction to every gr-semistable orthogonal filtration, beyond the allowed bundle and connection foundations.

items.title: Low-degree branched projective structures form a universal affine bundle over a family of branching classes
items.published_title: Low-degree branched projective structures form a universal affine bundle over a family of branching classes
items.author: Billon, Gustave
items.difficulty_reason: The affine-bundle conclusion depends on constructing relative branched projective atlases with prescribed branching class and identifying their differences through a relative Schwarzian equation. The new core forms an obstruction section via the Leray exact sequence, proves local holomorphic nonemptiness, and constructs a tautological universal family compatible with pullback. Serre duality supplies only the final low-degree vanishing; it does not supply these relative geometric constructions, which are retained in full and exceed ordinary PhD qualification exercises.

items.title: Uniform exponential moments for first-exit particles of nondegenerate critical branching random walks with exponential offspring moments
items.published_title: Uniform exponential moments for first-exit particles of nondegenerate critical branching random walks with exponential offspring moments
items.author: Amine Asselah; Bruno Schapira
items.difficulty_reason: A BGW exponential-moment bound by itself does not control the number of particles frozen at a spatial boundary, because repeated interior generations and spatial displacement remain coupled. The authors first contract the killed tree in generation blocks, then construct a quadratic spatial martingale linking its occupation to the frozen boundary population and control that martingale with the new killed-occupation estimate. The exit-probability and exponential-expansion steps then give the uniform squared-radius and sharper interior-start assertions, beyond standard BGW and random-walk prerequisites.

items.difficulty_reason: H3 residual after the explicitly cited growth-indicator, finite proximality and Morse background: construct a quasi-geodesic semigroup with bounded two-sided correction, then refine exponentially many long elements into equal-length, free, uniformly diagonalizable generators with a common nearby splitting without losing growth entropy. items.published_title: Automatic split-generation and the quantum-cohomology factor from a smooth Lagrangian endomorphism algebra
items.author: Jack Smith
items.difficulty_reason: The seven conclusions are connected by the Shklyarov pairing, open–closed isometry, weak proper Calabi–Yau duality, and the Hochschild module action. The proof constructs the two-sided quantum-cohomology factors Q and Q-perp, identifies the closed–open kernel, and proves split-generation by the resulting idempotent through Abouzaid’s criterion. Smoothness, Morita invariance and these categorical compatibility arguments exceed ordinary PhD qualifying-exam symplectic topology, while their cited standard foundations are kept distinct from Smith’s source-local construction.

items.published_title: Geometric l-adic local systems on punctured smooth projective finite-field curves that no family of abelian varieties can generate
items.author: Paul Brommer-Wierig; Yeuk Hay Joshua Lam
items.difficulty_reason: Tensor generation by abelian families permits large slopes in their tensor objects, so raw slopes of the proposed local system do not provide the required obstruction. The authors pass to the functorial monodromy Lie-local-system, bound its slopes through a Tannakian quotient, and apply that new obstruction to the ordinary invariant-summand/adjoint examples in every characteristic before pulling back to the chosen curve. This generation obstruction is the remaining nonroutine step; the source's monodromy, ordinarity, comparison and Hodge inputs are precise prior prerequisites, and the final slope tables alone are not the difficulty rationale.

items.author: David Meyer
items.difficulty_reason: Beyond ordinary elliptic, Newtonian-potential and fixed-test-function variational prerequisites, the proof reconstructs the unbounded axisymmetric no-swirl fluid from weighted potentials and circulation streamfunctions. It proves their shape differentiability and locally uniform decay, justifies all pressure integrations at infinity, and identifies the circulation-force, gyroscopic, added-inertia and Christoffel contributions. This complete volume-preserving nonrigid fluid–solid reduction is beyond ordinary doctoral PDE qualifiers.

items.title: Vanishing minimal volume entropy for finite simplicial complexes with fiber growth strictly below the codimension ratio
items.published_title: Vanishing minimal volume entropy for finite simplicial complexes with fiber growth strictly below the codimension ratio
items.author: Ivan Babenko; Stéphane Sabourau
items.difficulty_reason: Fiberwise contraction does not by itself control entropy because short loops can repeatedly leave fibers while the metric degenerates. The authors construct face-coherent Lipschitz retractions on uniform neighborhoods and prove an arc-to-edge deformation with a length constant independent of the collapsing parameter. They then count the interleaved long edges and fiber paths using subgroup growth to obtain the required entropy bound, which combines with volume scaling to give the strict codimension threshold.

items.title: Arbitrary-order depletion-layer expansion for the continuous half-space Stokes model with smooth compactly supported data up to the interface
items.published_title: Arbitrary-order depletion-layer expansion for the continuous half-space Stokes model with smooth compactly supported data up to the interface
items.author: David Gérard-Varet; Amina Mecherbet
items.difficulty_reason: After standard half-space Stokes solvability/regularity and thin-layer Poincare/trace estimates, the remaining construction couples bulk profiles with rescaled depletion-layer profiles through velocity, normal-divergence and stress matching at every fixed order. The human proof adds a normal-component term at order m+2 plus a global divergence corrector so the truncated composite field is continuous and solenoidal with a controllable interface stress residual. These choices are needed before the energy estimate yields the stated O(epsilon^(m+1)) homogeneous H1 remainder; constants may depend on m and no uniform-in-m bound is asserted.

items.published_title: Ergodicity of nonzero centered linear real extensions of every ergodic symmetric interval exchange, including connections
items.author: Przemysław Berk; Frank Trujillo; Hao Wu
items.difficulty_reason: After standard IET induction, recurrence and the Conze-Fraczek essential-value criterion, the proof must preserve reversal symmetry and track induced centers even when the ergodic IET has connections. It changes the induction center twice to rebalance high-measure thin towers and wide bases, obtaining positive-mass rigidity towers with a quantitative return bound. The new effective criterion then builds subtowers realizing an interval of essential values, while antisymmetric cancellation controls the centered linear Birkhoff sums; neither generic Rauzy-Veech induction nor the final mean-value estimate alone supplies this construction.

items.difficulty_reason: The generators have noncommuting quadratic relations, so centrality cannot be read off from a commutative presentation. The author establishes a confluent ordered monomial basis, changes its filtered leading terms to include the Casimir, and analyzes commutators of a hypothetical extra central element. A minimal-degree argument then removes every possible leading term, yielding a complete center classification rather than merely exhibiting known central elements.

items.author: Gábor Somlai
items.difficulty_reason: After the precise prior cyclic spectral/tiling reductions, positive prime-coset decomposition, cube rule and Coven--Meyerowitz tiling criterion, the author still proves a modular projection lemma and combines it with a complete cardinality analysis. The coupled spectrum graphs and projected coset restrictions must simultaneously control the p-squared coordinate and both other prime directions to force a tiling. That residual structural classification is nonroutine rather than direct cyclotomic substitution, giving a conservative H1.

items.title: For rational 1 < k < c < k squared, SAT has no eventually successful nonuniform refuter of size n to c against co-nondeterministic circuits of size n to k
items.published_title: For rational 1 < k < c < k squared, SAT has no eventually successful nonuniform refuter of size n to c against co-nondeterministic circuits of size n to k
items.author: Lijie Chen; Jiatu Li; Igor C. Oliveira
items.difficulty_reason: A refuter output need not reveal the truth of its SAT instance efficiently, so a single use of the refuter does not yield the desired contradiction. The proof recursively packages the complement of a longer instance into a smaller-input circuit, applies refuters across a shrinking sequence of lengths, and resolves the final instance using a hardcoded truth table. It coordinates the opposing input-size and refuter-size constraints using c < k squared, controlling all stages and the final table so that the constructed deciding circuit is itself small enough to be refuted.

Producing the object alone does not satisfy the theorem.

items.published_title: Composition of rigidified relative dualizing complexes for flat morphisms
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The proof constructs the required rigidification for the tensor-product candidate through two successive diagonals. It combines exact-support derived Hom, tensor compatibility and flat base change, then repeats the construction on diagonal neighbourhoods in the nonseparated case. The rigidifying map is an actual extra construction beyond algebraic tensor transitivity.

Both the fundamental class construction and the converse smoothness criterion are substantive obligations.

items.published_title: Deligne systems represent derived Hom after restriction to an open subscheme
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The proof reduces to Ext of coherent sheaves, then proves both injectivity and surjectivity by induction on Ext degree. Artin-Rees controls the changing kernels and powers of the boundary ideal while coherent extensions kill and lift extension classes. The pro-system comparison is a long exactness-and-lifting argument.

Joint Casimir and weight spectra then identify the precise irreducible principal and strange summands, rather than treating the representation as a single ordinary tensor product.

These two constructions reduce coherence of an arbitrary coherent sheaf to its associated integral components.

The normalization-and-depth construction is the nonroutine content.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: Recovering the ring map on global sections is only the first step: the proof must identify the inverse-image functor on every affine etale representable. Polynomial equalizer presentations and local maps of strictly henselian stalks produce these identifications, whose functoriality and compatibility with structure sheaves must be verified.

items.difficulty_reason: Perron-Frobenius positivity alone does not identify which irreducible flavor representation contains a many-fermion sector minimum. The author constructs a fermionic sign basis for hopping, exchange and pair hopping, and a compact trial configuration whose row symmetrization and column antisymmetrization isolate one Young type. Positive overlap and uniqueness then identify the relative ground multiplet, and a shared-weight comparison proves strict energy ordering under diagram dominance.

items.title: Joint time-evolution orbits of the periodic binary box-ball system with every amplitude one through N present and positive vacancy numbers are finite integer tori with explicit internal-symmetry period matrices and translation velocities
items.published_title: Joint time-evolution orbits of the periodic binary box-ball system with every amplitude one through N present and positive vacancy numbers are finite integer tori with explicit internal-symmetry period matrices and translation velocities
items.author: Taichiro Takagi
items.difficulty_reason: Knowing the inverse scattering bijection does not identify joint evolution orbits when solitons of equal amplitude have internal periods. The author stratifies extended riggings by exact cyclic stabilizers, constructs commuting twisted slide and translation actions, and proves that the internal-stabilizer action is a rigging-independent period lattice. He transports the quotient back through the scattering map and matches every time evolution with its explicit integer velocity.

items.published_title: For closed oriented three-manifolds with a fixed distinguished two-tetrahedron framed-knot chain and nondegenerate Euclidean geometrization, acyclicity and normalized geometric torsion are preserved by relative triangulation changes
items.author: Jérôme Dubois; Igor G. Korepanov; Evgeniy V. Martyushev
items.difficulty_reason: The construction must match infinitesimal vertex, edge-length, deficit-angle and rotation maps into a symmetric acyclic complex, rather than apply torsion to a given cellular complex. The author proves the relative Pachner connectivity and tracks the changing maximal minors through both the two-to-three and one-to-four moves. Exact edge-length and oriented-volume factors cancel against the normalization, while the same nonvanishing minors preserve acyclicity.

items.title: For every n at least three, the explicit corner monomial map intertwines all Kashiwara operators on horizontal regular partitions for affine sl(n), including odd n
items.published_title: For every n at least three, the explicit corner monomial map intertwines all Kashiwara operators on horizontal regular partitions for affine sl(n), including odd n
items.author: Peter Tingley
items.difficulty_reason: The boundary monomial product does not automatically preserve the operator selecting a surviving bracket in a partition signature. The proof translates the forbidden horizontal hook condition into precise height and content inequalities for addable and removable boxes, then proves that the monomial and partition signatures differ only by canceling adjacent pairs. A separate local corner update identifies the resulting monomial factor for each selected box, completing the explicit intertwining for even and odd n.

items.title: Discrete brane-labelled open and closed arc-graph correlators respect all window gluings for basic ordinary Frobenius systems with commutative closed algebra and Euler compatibility
items.published_title: Discrete brane-labelled open and closed arc-graph correlators respect all window gluings for basic ordinary Frobenius systems with commutative closed algebra and Euler compatibility
items.author: Ralph M. Kaufmann
items.difficulty_reason: Open window gluing can change the number of complementary regions and create labelled punctures, so the closed Frobenius contraction formula alone does not provide an action. The author defines weights for decorated boundary pieces and punctures and checks every local non-self and self-gluing topology. The new lone-window cases require the projection and Euler compatibility identities, with explicit contractions producing exactly the required Euler and puncture factors.

items.difficulty_reason: An arbitrary module sheaf must be reconstructed from global sections, not merely checked on a given affine presentation. The proof reduces every etale object to finite local etale algebras and uses semilinear Galois descent twice to handle both Galois and non-Galois residue extensions.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The proof must construct a canonical antisymmetrization section in the d-fold tensor power that glues despite line-bundle ambiguity in local splitting modules. Its right ideal gives a globally defined splitting module of the precise rank, yielding an endomorphism-algebra description without assuming d! is invertible.

items.title: Finite-dimensional top coherent cohomology of separated finite-type schemes over a field
items.published_title: Finite-dimensional top coherent cohomology of separated finite-type schemes over a field
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The statement does not assume properness, so standard proper cohomology finiteness cannot be applied directly. The proof combines induction on dimension and coherent devissage with Chow modification, relative ampleness and a lower-dimensional cokernel, then obtains a surjection from cohomology on a projective compactification.

items.difficulty_reason: Classical dispersive norms are poorly behaved under the Moyal product, so standard small-data NLS scattering cannot be applied without constructing another analytic framework. The author obtains uniform oscillator-matrix propagation bounds by rewriting the heat kernel as Jacobi polynomials and applying a precisely stated uniform weighted bound. New weighted matrix-product and polynomial Lipschitz estimates then verify every hypothesis of the abstract nonlinear scattering theorem, yielding a concrete scattering space and the stated degree restrictions.

items.difficulty_reason: The authored proof translates failure of a bounded-round disjoint-disjunction search into consistency of a nonstandard universal-arithmetic theory via KPT witnessing. items.title: A surjective separated etale map of algebraic spaces yields an integral alternating Cech spectral sequence on unordered distinct-point configurations with sign local coefficients
items.published_title: A surjective separated etale map of algebraic spaces yields an integral alternating Cech spectral sequence on unordered distinct-point configurations with sign local coefficients
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The construction replaces ordered etale Cech intersections by unordered configurations while retaining integral coefficients and the sign local system. Its proof must identify exterior-power sheaves with configuration-space sign coinvariants, build the character line sheaf on a finite-group quotient, and compare two injective double-complex spectral sequences. This geometric and derived construction goes beyond a routine Cech-cover computation, and does not assume exactness of group anti-invariants.

items.title: For finite loop-free quivers with nonzero framing and a stability face with both zero and positive coordinates, IC pushforward to zero stability has regular-stratum multiplicities equal to highest-weight Levi branching
items.published_title: For finite loop-free quivers with nonzero framing and a stability face with both zero and positive coordinates, IC pushforward to zero stability has regular-stratum multiplicities equal to highest-weight Levi branching
items.author: Hiraku Nakajima
items.difficulty_reason: The usual quiver-variety representation theorem does not identify which intersection-cohomology summands appear after an intermediate stability face is contracted to zero stability. The author compares the two semismall convolution algebras and their decomposition-theorem multiplicity spaces, then uses the face-stratum direct-sum diagram to exclude nonregular supports from the relevant branching coefficients. This geometric comparison turns restriction to the Levi algebra into a precise regular-stratum IC multiplicity formula.

items.title: The two-sided discrete Schrodinger operator with the authored complex interface has a bounded compact Green inverse for real uniformly positive confining potentials and phase from zero inclusive to pi over two exclusive
items.published_title: The two-sided discrete Schrodinger operator with the authored complex interface has a bounded compact Green inverse for real uniformly positive confining potentials and phase from zero inclusive to pi over two exclusive
items.author: Ebru Ergun
items.difficulty_reason: A positive potential alone does not supply a Green kernel compatible with the complex impulse matching at the missing lattice sites. The author constructs two independent half-line square-summable solutions through nested fractional-linear disks and weighted energy identities, then proves that the resulting infinite Green series maps the whole sequence Hilbert space into the operator domain. A uniform inverse bound and a separate potential-weighted tail estimate yield compactness without assuming Hermitian spectral theory.

items.title: Finite etale covers of proper schemes over henselian local rings are determined by the closed fibre
items.published_title: Finite etale covers of proper schemes over henselian local rings are determined by the closed fibre
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: One must algebraize the entire compatible infinitesimal tower of a finite etale cover and establish full faithfulness through graph lifting. The proof then uses approximation of solutions over the completion and a directed-limit reduction through henselian Noetherian G-rings to handle an arbitrary henselian local base.

a) 实质要求。条目头 b8-dump.txt:3472–3473（3472「### B8-23  env=lemma  label=lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian」；3473「### file=pione.tex  statement_lines=[1621, 1630]  proof_lines=[1632, 1746]  proof_bytes=5561」）。题面 dump 3475–3484（3474 = 「---- STATEMENT ----」标记）= 源 pione.tex 1621–1630（10 行），逐字：「\begin{lemma}」/「\label{lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian}」/「Let $A$ be a henselian local ring. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $A$」/「with closed fibre $X_0$. Then the functor」/「$$」/「\textit{F\'Et}_X \to \textit{F\'Et}_{X_0},\quad」/「U \longmapsto U_0 = U \times_X X_0」/「$$」/「is an equivalence of categories.」/「\end{lemma}」。实质要求：对任意 henselian 局部环 $A$ 与 $A$ 上 proper 概型 $X$（闭纤维 $X_0$），证明「有限 étale 概型范畴」的截断函子 $U \mapsto U_0 = U \times_X X_0$ 是范畴等价。等价 = 两个方向：本质满（每个 $X_0$ 上有限 étale 的 $U_0$ 都来自某个 $X$ 上有限 étale 的 $U$）与全忠实（同态的双射）；这是 henselian 环上「形式对象代数化」的经典形态，通常由 SGA 1/EGA 的 hensel 理论得出。

The functor」…「defines an equivalence of categories」/「\{」/「\text{schemes }X\text{ \'etale over }S」/「\}」/「\leftrightarrow」/「\{」/「\text{schemes }X_0\text{ \'etale over }S_0」/「\}」——即 EGA IV 18.1.2（该定理自带的 \begin{reference} 逐字「\cite[IV, Theorem 18.1.2]{EGA}」）。即把 $U_0$ 沿 $X_0 \to X_n$（同底拓扑空间的加厚）搬运到 $X_n$ 的工具（原文以行间公式给出该等价：两端的对象分别是 $X$ 上 étale 的概型与 $X_0$ 上 étale 的概型）。

c) 本证明实际做了什么（逐段点名，给出决定性一步的归属）：
1) 「Essential surjectivity when $A$ is a complete local Noetherian ring.」（dump:3491–3517 / 源 1637–1663）决定性的一步在此，且整条被引：先「By \'Etale Morphisms, Theorem \ref{etale-theorem-remarkable-equivalence}」把「the category」/「of schemes \'etale over $X_0$」与「the category of schemes」/「\'etale over $X_n$」等同（dump:3493–3500）；再引 (ii) 型工具确认有限性（dump:3503–3504）；然后「Thus we may apply」/「Grothendieck's algebraization theorem」得到「there is a finite morphism $U \to X$ whose restriction」/「to $X_0$ recovers $U_0$」（dump:3506–3512；逐字形态见上文 (ii)）；最后「By More on Morphisms, Lemma」/「\ref{more-morphisms-lemma-check-smoothness-on-infinitesimal-nbhds}」得 $U_0$ 处 étale，并以 proper 性（「as $U$ is proper over $A$」）把 étale 性从 $U_0$ 提升到全 $U$。作者自己的动作只有这句「However, since every point of $U$ specializes to a point of $U_0$」(dump:3515)——一句紧化观察，用来补上最后一步。
2) 「Fully faithfulness when $A$ is a complete local Noetherian ring.」（dump:3520–3536 / 源 1666–1682）：把 $\varphi_0$ 取图 $\Gamma_{\varphi_0}$（dump:3525），「By essential surjectivity applied to $X = U \times_X V$ we find」$W$（dump:3528–3530，逐字见前引两行），再引 \ref{etale-lemma-finite-etale-one-point} 得邻域内同构，于是「Thus it is an isomorphism and the composition $\varphi : U \cong W \to V$」/「is the desired lift of $\varphi_0$.」——这一半的方向完全建立在刚刚（由被引件交付的）本质满之上。
3) 「Essential surjectivity when $A$ is a henselian local Noetherian G-ring.」（dump:3539–3563 / 源 1685–1709）：从完备情形得到 $X^\wedge$ 上的 $V$（依赖 1)），再用 Limits 三条把 $V$ 下降成某个 $A_i$ 上的 $U_i$，再引 Artin 逼近（iii）把 $A_i \to A^\wedge$ 的「解」逼近回 $A$，并以「(as $11 > 1$)」把整数阈值 $11$ 与「which gives the same closed point as the original map」对齐（dump:3559–3561 / 源 1705–1707）。此段的承重机制 = (1) + Artin 逼近，均为被引。
4) 「Fully faithfulness when $A$ is a henselian local Noetherian G-ring.」（dump:3566–3568 / 源 1712–1714）全文逐字：「This can be deduced from essential surjectivity in exactly the same」/「manner as was done in the case that $A$ is complete Noetherian.」——即完全复述 2) 的论证，无新机制。
5) 「General case.」（dump:3571–3599 / 源 1717–1745）：$X \to \Spec(A)$ 写成 proper $X_i \to S_i$（$S_i$ 有限型于 $\mathbf{Z}$）的余滤极限（引 \ref{limits-lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation-noetherian}）；$A_i = \mathcal{O}_{S_i, s_i}$ 是 Noetherian 局部 G-ring（引 \ref{more-algebra-proposition-ubiquity-G-ring}）；$A = \colim A_i^h$（引 \ref{more-algebra-lemma-henselization-colimit}）且 $A_i^h$ 是 G-ring（引 \ref{more-algebra-lemma-henselization-G-ring}）；最后「The category of schemes finite \'etale over $X$ is the limit」/「of the category of schemes finite \'etale over」/「$X_i \times_{S_i} \Spec(A_i^h)$」（引 Limits 三条，dump:3590–3594），并逐字以「Thus we formally deduce the result for $X / \Spec(A)$」/「from the result for the $(X_i \times_{S_i} \Spec(A_i^h)) / \Spec(A_i^h)$」/「which we dealt with above.」收口。
⚠️ 如实标注（不改判、但必须记下）：第 5) 段的整段论证与源 more-algebra.tex 中既有的 Lemma \ref{lemma-henselian-local-limit-G-rings}（陈述 12675–12679，证明 12681–12689）逐句同构——该被引件证明逐字：「Write $A = \colim A_i$ as a filtered colimit of finite type」/「$\mathbf{Z}$-algebras. Let $\mathfrak p_i$ be the prime ideal of」/「$A_i$ lying under $\mathfrak m$. We may replace $A_i$ by the」/「localization of $A_i$ at $\mathfrak p_i$. Then $A_i$ is a」/「Noetherian local G-ring (Proposition \ref{proposition-ubiquity-G-ring}).」/「By Lemma \ref{lemma-henselization-colimit}」/「we see that $A = \colim A_i^h$. By」/「Lemma \ref{lemma-henselization-G-ring}」/「the rings $A_i^h$ are G-rings.」，与本条 dump:3575–3584 逐字对应。即「一般情形」这一步的骨架在本项目来源库中已作为引理现成存在，作者（本条所在的 Stacks 章节）沿用它并接上极限下降。

d) 为何不是 H3。整条证明没有任何自造对象、自造机制或自组织归约：(1) 决定性的存在性（本质满）在完备情形由 Grothendieck 代数化定理（ii）＋ 同底加厚等价（i）交付；(2) henselian G-ring 情形由 Artin 逼近（iii）交付；(3) 一般情形由极限呈现＋极限下降（iv 组）交付，且骨架与被引的 \ref{lemma-henselian-local-limit-G-rings} 逐句同构；(4) 全忠实两个情形中，一个是从本质满「完全一样地」推出（dump:3566–3568 逐字自陈），另一个只是在完备情形把 $\varphi_0$ 取图再引单点引理（\ref{etale-lemma-finite-etale-one-point}）。证明自己承担的部分 = 把上述被引件按「完备 Noetherian → henselian G-ring → 一般」三段拼装，并核对各处假设（proper 性、有限性、$U$ 的性质、极限情形的可下降性）。按档位口径，这属于「拼装已有结果／核对更大结果的假设」，且 H3 硬判据所要求的「决定性一步由本证明承担」不成立（本质满与逼近两步的机制整体外借），故判 H2，而非 H3。

须如实标注的反方向读法（不改变本判档）：若把「一般情形」的极限论证单独认定为决定性的一步，可主张它由本证明完成（把一个任意 henselian 局部环写成 henselian G-ring 的余滤余极限、并把两边的有限 étale 范畴都识别为极限范畴），其中含自组织的归约与极限论证，据此可读作 H3。本文不采此读法，理由：该段与既存的 \ref{lemma-henselian-local-limit-G-rings} 逐句同构（见 c) 末的 ⚠️），其每一步都是被引引理的直接应用（极限呈现、G-ring 无处不有、henselization 与余极限交换、极限下降），没有自造机制；且真正的结论性内容（有限 étale 范畴对余极限的相容性）也是被引的 Limits 三条直接给出的。

e) 档位外的一处如实提示：本条的 proper 性出现在假设中（源 1623「Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $A$」、dump:3477），证明中两次把它当作工具使用（dump:3506「as $X_0$ is proper over $A/\mathfrak m$」、dump:3515「as $U$ is proper over $A$」），并未反过来由证明建立 proper 性；这不影响判档，但说明本条是「在一个已经很强的几何假设下」的拼接式论证。

items.title: Etaleness of inertia invariants for finite group actions on arbitrary rings
items.published_title: Etaleness of inertia invariants for finite group actions on arbitrary rings
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The proof must show the invariant-ring map is etale at a selected prime without normality or finite-type assumptions. Etale localization splits the integral fibre, and a further equivariant clopen refinement makes the group permute factors; the inertia subgroup then identifies a factor of the full invariant ring.
