research_reviews.difficulty_reason:
实质要求：设有限群 $G$ 作用于环 $R$，$\mathfrak q \subset R$ 为素理想，惯性群 $I = \{\sigma \in G \mid \sigma(\mathfrak q) = \mathfrak q \text{ and } \sigma \bmod \mathfrak q = \text{id}_\mathfrak q\}$，断言「Then $R^G \to R^I$ is \'etale at $R^I \cap \mathfrak q$.」（statement 2664–2673，结句 2672）。$G, R, \mathfrak q, I$ 全由题面给出，须证的是两个不变量子环之间映射在指定素点处的 étale 性——这是「惯性群控制商映射局部结构」的一般结构步，非平凡，但要证它只有两条腿：先允许 étale 局部化，再把情形裂开。

允许引用（逐条核对过）：证明开门即宣告策略「The strategy of the proof is to use \'etale localization to / reduce to the case where $R \to R^I$ is a local isomorphism at / $R^I \cap \mathfrak p$.」（2675–2677；原文如此：命题作 $R^G \to R^I$，此句作 $R \to R^I$，且 $\mathfrak p$ 此处尚未定义，直到 2709 才出现「Let $\mathfrak p = R^G \cap \mathfrak q$.」；按最终归约读，本句所指应为 $R^G \to R^I$ 在 $R^I \cap \mathfrak q$ 处局部同构，因 2774 的 $R^G = (A_1)^I \subset R^I = (A_1)^I \times (A')^I$ 恰使该映射在 $R^I \cap \mathfrak q$ 处成为同构）。随后引用 More on Algebra, Lemma base-change-invariants（2669、2672–2675，平坦基变换下不变量）、同章 Lemma \ref{lemma-inertia-base-change}（2671，「By Lemma \ref{lemma-inertia-base-change} the group $I$ does not change.」）、More on Algebra, Lemma one-orbit / one-orbit-geometric（2693–2697，$G$ 在 $\mathfrak p$ 上素理想间传递、纤维有限、剩余域扩张代数正规）、Descent, Lemma smooth-permanence（2687–2688，étale 的下降/永久性）。归约的硬核整块被引：「Thus we may apply / More on Morphisms, / Lemma \ref{more-morphisms-lemma-etale-makes-integral-split} / to the integral ring map $R^G \to R$ and the prime $\mathfrak p$.」（2698–2701，被引件名见 2717），紧接着「Combined with the claim above we reduce to the case where / $R = A_1 \times \ldots \times A_n$ with each $A_i$ having a single / prime $\mathfrak q_i$ lying over $\mathfrak p$ such that the / residue field extensions $\kappa(\mathfrak q_i)/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ / are purely inseparable.」（2702–2706）。

必须由本证明完成的部分：(a) 补上被引 Descent 引理所需的中间环节——étale 基变换下 $A \otimes_{R^G} R^I = (A \otimes_{R^G} R)^I$ 与 cartesian 方块，从而断言「if the result / holds for the action of $G$ on $A \otimes_{R^G} R$ and some prime / $\mathfrak q'$ of $A \otimes_{R^G} R$ lying over $\mathfrak q$, then / the result is true.」（2662–2665，方块与收口 2677–2689）；(b) 自造的 G-稳定化：乘积分解未必被 $G$ 置换，于是「Since $G$ is finite, we can refine this covering / by a finite disjoint union decomposition / $\Spec(R) = \coprod_{j \in J} W_j$ by open / and closed subsets $W_j$, such that for all $j \in J$ there exists / a $j' \in J$ with $\sigma(W_j) = W_{j'}$.」（2716–2721），再用 $\Spec(R) \to \Spec(R^G)$ 的闭性把不碰 $\mathfrak q_i$ 的分支经主局部化砍掉（2721–2731；作者自注「we suggest the reader think this through for themselves, perhaps / using idempotents instead of topology.」，2712–2714）；(c) 收口计算：纯不可分剩余域使 $I = D$，$G$ 的传递性给出 $[G:I] = n$ 与 $A_i = \sigma_i(A_1)$，于是「It follows that / $$ / R^G = (A_1)^I. / $$」（2755–2758，2774），$R^G \to R^I$ 成为直因子含入（即幂等元局部化）因而 étale（2759–2760）。

三条门槛：(i) 只部分满足——让整个论证可能的裂开归约由被引 More on Morphisms 引理承担，作者自己承认是引用后的产物（2733–2734：「Thus we may assume we have a product decomposition / $R = A_1 \times \ldots \times A_n$ compatible with $G$-action …」）；(ii) 弱成立——结论确有结构意义（惯性群不变量是商映射的 étale 邻域），但它不是某节冠名主定理，而是通向下一节 ramification theory 的链条一环，\end{proof} 之后立刻服务下一条：「The following lemma generalizes / More on Algebra, Lemma \ref{more-algebra-lemma-inertial-invariants-unramified}.」（2781–2782，对应下一条 lemma-inertial-invariants-unramified）；(iii) 不成立——它是专著（Stacks 项目 'Fundamental Groups of Schemes' 章，pione.tex，section \label{section-group-actions-integral}「Group actions and integral closure」，2580）里的工具引理，机制全用标准件（étale 局部化、平坦基变换不变量、幂等元/主局部化、单轨道传递性），无自造对象（题面已给 $G,R,\mathfrak q,I$）或新机制。故封顶 H2，不判 H3；也不是 H1，因为证明确有一段实质装配（étale 局部化永久性断言与 G-稳定化论证）不是纯引用或纯验证。

items.title: Thompson’s group T has quadratic Dehn function
items.published_title: Thompson’s group T has quadratic Dehn function
items.author: Matteo Migliorini
items.difficulty_reason: The usual infinite-presentation normal form may be much longer than the word norm. The author constructs finite-generator normal forms with at most one rotation letter and linear length control, then reduces all two- and three-rotation triangular loops through the interval stabilizer and explicit conjugation relations with quadratic area. This new efficient dynamical normal-form and filling construction is beyond ordinary qualifying presentation manipulations; Guba’s theorem for F is an explicit prerequisite.

items.title: Faltings annihilator theorem for local cohomology
items.published_title: Faltings annihilator theorem for local cohomology
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a global annihilator by a double induction on cohomological degree and dimension-function strata. Spectral-sequence filtrations control successive powers of annihilators, and finite dualizing Ext supports produce uniform choices. The converse locates a minimal failing depth-codimension pair and proves its local cohomology cannot be annihilated.

items.title: Essential surjectivity of the derived functor to a Serre quotient
items.published_title: Essential surjectivity of the derived functor to a Serre quotient
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The proof strictifies a complex in the quotient category in both directions: pushouts handle nonnegative degrees and pullbacks handle negative degrees. It must then replace terms by finite sums of images and intersections of kernels so the lifted differentials square to zero in the original category. This is an actual lifting construction for unbounded quotient complexes.

items.title: Existence of unbounded left derived functors under exact sequential colimits
items.published_title: Existence of unbounded left derived functors under exact sequential colimits
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The proof builds a compatible sequence of bounded-above resolutions whose colimit resolves an arbitrary complex. It handles the essential difficulty that a morphism of colimit resolutions need not come from levelwise maps, using common bounded resolutions and compatible cohomology comparisons. Exactness and preservation of sequential colimits then yield the desired quasi-isomorphism.

items.difficulty_reason: The authored proof forces any stabilising birational morphism to blow up every point of a minimal destabilising orbit, using locally stable compositions and total transforms, then turns that factorisation into bounded termination and uniqueness of the dynamical model. This combines surface birational geometry with orbit-level algebraic stability beyond routine graduate qualifying material.

items.title: Existence and isomorphism of Postnikov systems under Hom vanishing
items.published_title: Existence and isomorphism of Postnikov systems under Hom vanishing
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The proof inductively extends a totalization tower and identifies its obstruction as a composite into an earlier cone. Iterated distinguished triangles and the shifted Hom bounds annihilate that obstruction; the stronger bounds then lift the identity to an isomorphism of systems. This is an obstruction-theoretic existence theorem for totalizing complexes in abstract triangulated categories.

items.author: Olivier Haution
items.difficulty_reason: The proof must globalize local two-dimensional resolutions while controlling every point lying over codimension at most two. It constructs a global blowup center through scheme-theoretic images and verifies its local models using flat base change and regularity descent. Passing from normal to reduced quasi-excellent schemes additionally requires finite-normalization and codimension control, rather than a direct invocation of local resolution.

items.title: Curvature criterion for lifting first-order formal projective-metrizability jets to second order
items.published_title: Curvature criterion for lifting first-order formal projective-metrizability jets to second order
items.author: Ioan Bucataru; Zoltan Muzsnay
items.difficulty_reason: A curvature compatibility condition is not sufficient for jet prolongation merely because it is necessary for an actual solution. The authors compute the prolonged projective-metrizability symbol and its cokernel, construct five explicit Spencer obstruction components, and use a vertical-structure preserving connection to identify their values. Four components cancel by Frolicher-Nijenhuis commutators while the remaining tau4 component is exactly the nonlinear-connection curvature obstruction, giving both directions of the finite-order lift criterion.

items.title: Supercritical normalized solutions for the critical fractional Kirchhoff-Schrodinger-Poisson system
items.published_title: Supercritical normalized solutions for the critical fractional Kirchhoff-Schrodinger-Poisson system
items.author: Yu-Qin Zhao; Jia-Feng Liao
items.difficulty_reason: The critical fractional Sobolev embedding remains noncompact even in the radial space, and the prescribed mass constraint can be lost by a weak Palais-Smale limit. The authors develop the mass-preserving fiber geometry and Pohozaev constraint for the Kirchhoff and nonlocal Poisson terms, obtain a minimax sequence with an additional vanishing Pohozaev condition, and derive a critical energy bound excluding critical concentration. Their local estimates force a negative limiting Lagrange multiplier and recover the full mass with strong convergence, which is substantially beyond a routine variational existence proof.

items.title: General energy decay for a coupled viscoelastic wave system with a single memory term
items.published_title: General energy decay for a coupled viscoelastic wave system with a single memory term
items.author: Houda Fadel; Djamila Benterki; Salim A. Messaoudi
items.difficulty_reason: Only the first wave is directly damped by memory, so positivity of the total energy alone does not control the undamped second wave or yield a general kernel-dependent decay rate. The authors assemble several cross and memory perturbations into a Lyapunov functional, balance coupling constants under alpha<sqrt(l)/Cp, then use both first- and second-order energy to derive a nonlinear convexity bound for the memory tail. Converting that bound into the inverse-G2 rate for a general nonlinear relaxation function is a nonroutine residual stability argument beyond standard wave energy estimates.

【题面与出处】b9-dump.txt:758–759 条目头（第758行『### B9-06  env=lemma  label=lemma-galois-inertia』；第759行『### file=more-algebra.tex  statement_lines=[33250, 33281]  proof_lines=[33283, 33406]  proof_bytes=5395』）。源文件 more-algebra.tex（本地 Stacks master 快照 raw/stacks-a04446e57ec1fbc252a871afcec7752fb2807b14，39222 行）33171–33172 行 \section{Galois extensions and ramification}（\label{section-ramification}）之下，label lemma-galois-inertia（tag 09EE，tags/tags:11897），statement 源 33250–33281（32 行），proof 源 33283–33406（124 行、5395 字节）。

【题面】设 $A$ 为分式域 $K$ 的离散赋值环，$L/K$ 有限 Galois、Galois 群 $G$，$B$ 为 $A$ 在 $L$ 中的整闭包，$\mathfrak m \subset B$ 极大理想，$I$ 为 $\mathfrak m$ 的惯性群。断言（源 33255–33258 逐字；引文中的『/』表示原文换行处）：『The inertia group $I$ of $\mathfrak m$ / sits in a canonical exact sequence / $$ / 1 \to P \to I \to I_t \to 1 / $$』，并给出六条：(1) 源 33273–33278 逐字『P = \{\sigma \in I \mid \sigma|_{\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2} = \text{id}_{\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2}\} / = / \{\sigma \in D \mid \sigma \text{ acts trivially on }\text{Gr}_\mathfrak m(B)\}』；(2) $P \trianglelefteq D$；(3) $\kappa_A$ 特征 $p>0$ 时 $P$ 是 $p$-群、特征 $0$ 时 $P=\{1\}$（源 33270–33272）；(4) $I_t$ 循环、阶为整数 $e$ 的素于 $p$ 部分；(5) 有典范同构 $\theta : I_t \to \mu_e(\kappa(\mathfrak m))$；(6) $\kappa(m)$ 在 $A$ 的剩余域上可分时 $P = \{\sigma \in D \mid \sigma|_{B/\mathfrak m^2} = \text{id}_{B/\mathfrak m^2}\}$。$e$ 的出处见源 33281 逐字『Here $e$ is the integer of Lemma \ref{lemma-galois-conclusion}.』；$D$、$I$ 的定义在同节 Definition \ref{definition-decomposition-inertia}（源 33204–33216，tag 09EC）：$D = \{\sigma \in G \mid \sigma(\mathfrak m) = \mathfrak m\}$，$I$ 是 $D \to \text{Aut}(\kappa(\mathfrak m)/\kappa_A)$ 的核。

【允许引用什么】本证明明引的输入只提供框架与现成事实，无一条给出『正合列存在』『$\theta$ 存在』或『$P$ 是 $p$-群』：① $|G| = [L:K] = nef$ 与 $G$ 在极大理想集上传递、$|D| = ef$：Lemma \ref{lemma-galois-conclusion}（源 33191–33198，tag 09EB）与 Lemma \ref{lemma-galois}（源 33178–33184，tag 09EA，其证明又引 lemma-one-orbit），用于源 33284–33288；② $ef = |D| = |I| \cdot |\text{Aut}(\kappa(\mathfrak m)/\kappa)|$：Lemma \ref{lemma-galois-galois}（源 33223–33240，tag 09ED；其内容为 $\kappa(\mathfrak m)/\kappa$ 正规、$D \to \text{Aut}(\kappa(\mathfrak m)/\kappa)$ 满），用于源 33289–33292；③『$\text{Aut}(\kappa(\mathfrak m)/\kappa)$ 的阶与 $f$ 相差 $p$ 的幂』：Fields, Lemma \ref{fields-lemma-normal-and-automorphisms} 与 Fields, Definition \ref{fields-definition-insep-degree} 之后的讨论（源 33294–33299），据此得『$|I|$ 的素于 $p$ 部分 $= e$ 的素于 $p$ 部分』（源 33300–33301）；④『$\mu_e(\kappa(\mathfrak m))$ 循环、阶至多为 $e$ 的素于 $p$ 部分』：Fields, Section \ref{fields-section-roots-of-1}（源 33340–33342）；⑤ 形式 étale 判别：Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-characterize-separable-algebraic-field-extensions}（源 33394–33396）；⑥ 背景事实：$\pi_A = u\pi_C^e$（源 33306，来自本节之前的 DVR 讨论，源 33175–33176 指向 Section \ref{section-discrete-valuation-rings}）、$\text{Gr}_\mathfrak m(B)$ 由 $\text{Gr}^1_\mathfrak m(B)$ 在 $\text{Gr}^0_\mathfrak m(B)$ 上生成（源 33352–33354，由分次环定义立得）。一句话：被引件给的是 $e/f/n$ 框架、$|\text{Aut}|$ 与 $f$ 差 $p$ 幂的算术、$\mu_e$ 的循环性、可分情形的形式 étale 工具。

【必须由本证明完成的部分（具体做法 + 原文定位）】(a) 自造核心对象 $\theta$（源 33304–33322）：令 $C = B_\mathfrak m$，取 uniformizer $\pi_A \in A$、$\pi_C \in C$，写 $\pi_A = u\pi_C^e$（$u$ 为 $C$ 中单位，源 33306）；对 $\sigma \in I$ 写 $\sigma(\pi_C) = \theta_\sigma \pi_C$（源 33307–33308），由源 33309–33312 的逐字计算『\pi_A = \sigma(\pi_A) = \sigma(u) (\theta_\sigma \pi_C)^e / = \sigma(u) \theta_\sigma^e \pi_C^e = \frac{\sigma(u)}{u} \theta_\sigma^e \pi_A』得 $\sigma(u)\theta_\sigma^e = u$，又因 $\sigma \in I$ 在剩余域上平凡故 $\sigma(u) \equiv u \bmod \mathfrak m_C$，于是 $\overline{\theta}_\sigma$ 是 $e$ 次单位根（源 33313–33316），由此得到映射（源 33317–33322，编号 \ref{equation-inertia-character}）$\theta : I \longrightarrow \mu_e(\kappa(\mathfrak m)), \sigma \mapsto \overline{\theta}_\sigma$。(b) 证 $\theta$ 是群同态且与 $\pi_C$ 的选取无关（源 33323–33337）：$\tau(\sigma(\pi_C)) = \tau(\theta_\sigma)\theta_\tau\pi_C$ 给出 $\theta_{\tau\sigma} = \tau(\theta_\sigma)\theta_\tau$，再用 $\tau \in I$ 在剩余域上平凡得 $\overline{\theta}_{\tau\sigma} = \overline{\theta}_\sigma \overline{\theta}_\tau$；换 uniformizer $\pi'_C = w\pi_C$ 时 $\theta'_\sigma = w^{-1}\sigma(w)\theta_\sigma$，与 $\theta_\sigma$ 在剩余域中同像。(c) 把 $P := \Ker(\theta)$ 与分歧滤链对上（源 33345–33356）：由 $\mathfrak m_C/\mathfrak m_C^2$ 由 $\pi_C$ 生成，$\overline{\theta}_\sigma = 1$ 当且仅当 $\sigma$ 在 $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ 上平凡，得 $P = \{\sigma \in I \mid \sigma|_{\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2} = \text{id}_{\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2}\}$；再由 $\text{Gr}_\mathfrak m(B)$ 由次数 1 部分生成（而 $I$ 在 $\text{Gr}^0_\mathfrak m = B/\mathfrak m$ 上平凡）提升为 $P = \{\sigma \in D \mid \sigma \text{ acts trivially on }\text{Gr}_\mathfrak m(B)\}$；于是 $P$ 是 $D \to \text{Aut}(\text{Gr}_\mathfrak m(B))$ 的核，得 (2)。(d) 证 $P$ 是 $p$-群（源 33363–33385）：对核中非平凡 $\sigma$ 先断言（源 33366–33368 逐字）『Then $\sigma - \text{id}$ / sends $\mathfrak m_C^i$ into $\mathfrak m_C^{i + 1}$ / for all $i$.』；取 $c$ 与 $i$ 使 $\sigma(c) - c \in \mathfrak m_C^i$ 而 $\sigma(c) - c \not \in \mathfrak m_C^{i + 1}$，用望远镜和（源 33372–33382）$0 = \sigma^m(c) - c = \sum\nolimits_{j = 0, \ldots, m - 1} \sigma^j(\sigma(c) - c) \equiv m(\sigma(c) - c) \bmod \mathfrak m_C^{i + 1}$，配合 DVR 性质得 $p \mid m$（源 33383–33385）。(e) (4)(5) 的阶数核算（源 33359–33361 逐字：『If we can prove (3), then parts (4) and (5) will follow as $I_t$ / will be isomorphic to $\mu_e(\kappa(\mathfrak m))$ as the arguments above show / that $|I_t| \geq |\mu_e(\kappa(\mathfrak m))|$.』）：借 (d) 得 $|I_t|$ 的素于 $p$ 部分 $= |I|$ 的素于 $p$ 部分 $= e$ 的素于 $p$ 部分，又 $I_t = I/\Ker\theta \hookrightarrow \mu_e$ 给出反向不等式，两面夹住得 $I_t \cong \mu_e$。(f) (6) 可分情形（源 33388–33405）：由 lemma-galois-galois 得 $f = |D/I|$、$|I| = e$（源 33389–33390）；$B/\mathfrak m^2$ 是 $\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ 的小扩张，形式 étale（引 Algebra）给出唯一右逆，从而有 $D$-等变分裂 $B/\mathfrak m^2 = \mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2 \oplus \kappa(\mathfrak m)$（源 33400–33402），立刻得到 $P = \{\sigma \in D \mid \sigma|_{B/\mathfrak m^2} = \text{id}_{B/\mathfrak m^2}\}$——此条是引用驱动的拼装，其中『唯一性 $\Rightarrow$ $D$-等变性』一步原文以『In other words』（源 33400）带过。

【判定：H3】按硬判据逐项看。决定性的一步是存在性/核心构造：典范正合列中的 $P$ 与被构造出来的惯性特征 $\theta$，以及 $I_t \cong \mu_e$ 的机制。这一步没有任何引用替代——被引件里没有一条给出 $\theta$ 的存在、$\Ker\theta$ 的分歧刻画或 $P$ 的 $p$-群性，三者都在本块内以自造手段完成：(a) 用 uniformizer 比值（$\sigma(\pi_C)/\pi_C$ 的剩余类）造对象 $\theta$；(b) 用分次环由次数 1 生成把 $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ 上的平凡性提升为 $\text{Gr}_\mathfrak m(B)$ 上的平凡性；(c) 用 $\sigma - \text{id}$ 的滤链作用加望远镜和这套自组织的 $p$-进论证证 $p$-群性。这属于判据的『建立』（自造对象、自造机制），而不是『核对』（按定义检查／拼装已有结果）：本证明不是在验证某个更大定理的假设，而是造出整节后续都要依赖的对象与结构——紧随其后的 Definition \ref{definition-wild-inertia}（源 33417–33428）逐字『We denote $\theta : I \to \mu_e(\kappa(\mathfrak m))$ the surjective map / (\ref{equation-inertia-character}) whose kernel is $P$ and which / induces the isomorphism $I_t \to \mu_e(\kappa(\mathfrak m))$.』；Lemma \ref{lemma-inertia-character} 的证明首句（源 33446）逐字『Recall the construction of $\theta$.』；Example \ref{example-counter-description-P}（源 33408–33415）用 $A = Z_2[t]_{(2)}$、$B = A[x]/(x^2 - t)$ 说明 (6) 去掉可分性即假；后文源 35425 又用它得惯性群可解。故『决定性的一步被引用则至多 H2』不适用。附带条款『断言双射/等价时若一个方向的机制整体来自被引件则整条至多 H2』亦不触发：(5) 的单射侧（$\Ker\theta = P$）由 (a)(c) 承担；满射侧（$I_t$ 的阶 $= e$ 的素于 $p$ 部分）确实借用了被引的素于 $p$ 部分核算与 $\mu_e$ 的循环性，但该方向必需的『$P$ 是 $p$-群』（否则无法把 $|I|$ 的素于 $p$ 部分搬到 $|I_t|$）由 (d) 在本块内证明，故无一个方向的机制『整体』来自被引件。难度定档：本条要在一般 DVR、剩余扩张可不可分均可的情形下给出惯性群的分歧结构（野惯性是 $p$-群、驯商 $\cong \mu_e$、野部分恰为在分次环上平凡者），属局部域/代数数论研究生教材之后的材料（Serre, Local Fields 中驯野分解一类结论），其核心构造（uniformizer 比值造特征）与非平凡的 $p$-进论证都超出通常数学博士资格考试对 Galois 分歧理论的要求范围（资格考一般止于 $efg = n$、$D/I \hookrightarrow \text{Aut}(\kappa(\mathfrak m)/\kappa)$ 一类的按定义核对）。故判 H3。

【笔误与原文瑕疵：逐字照抄并标注，未静默改正】① 源 33278（dump 789）在 (6) 中写『if $\kappa(m)$ is separable over the residue field of $A$.』，此处 $\kappa(m)$ 缺 \mathfrak，与全文 $\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ 不一致，系原文记法笔误，照抄并标注。② 源 33345、33384（dump 856、895）用 \Ker 而非 \ker（大写 K），原文如此照抄。③ 源 33383–33385 逐字『It follows that $p | m$ (or $m = 0$ if $p = 1$). Thus every element of the / kernel of $\theta$ has order divisible by $p$, i.e., $\Ker(\theta)$ / is a $p$-group.』——如实指出：字面上『每个元素的阶被 $p$ 整除』推不出『是 $p$-群』，标准补法是同一论证再施于 $\sigma^{p^a}$（阶的素于 $p$ 部分）以排除阶含素于 $p$ 的因子，原文未写出这半句（属省略/表述跳跃，结论本身正确，且该机制仍由本证明承担）；同句『(or $m = 0$ if $p = 1$)』是特征 $0$ 情形的极简写法（此时 $m \in \mathfrak m_C = 0$，即不存在这样的 $\sigma$，对应 (3) 后半 $P = \{1\}$）。④ 源 33288 用轨道-稳定化子得 $|D| = ef$（由 $|G| = nef$ 与 $n$ 个极大理想），原文未逐字写出 $n|D| = |G|$。⑤ 题面 (5) 用 $I_t$ 而未在题面内定义，$I_t$ 由正合列本身引入，其命名见后文 Definition \ref{definition-wild-inertia}（源 33423）。

items.difficulty_reason: The proof must compare the normal-cone definitions for nested centres with excess normal directions. items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: A valuation-ring reduction must preserve the original generic fibre and the closedness of the special point. e) 判档：①『$Y_d$ 仿射』所依赖的核心构造（有限局部自由 $T$ 与其截面 $T_i$）整体由被引件 morphisms-lemma-massage-finite（配 1127 的 pass-through-finite）交付，本证明零机制；②题面里『$Y_d$ 是开的』与最大值取到分别整体由被引件 lemma-semicontinuous-int-w、lemma-max-int-w 交付（1094–1096），且开性在 1159 还要再用一次；③本证明自留的份额是在上述被引结构上做权重记账＋不等式比较，把 $Y_d$ 识别为该结构的截面像之交（1155–1192）——这一步不是按定义核查、也不是拼装已陈述的等价，其两个方向的机制都在本证明内（$\subseteq$：等号成立迫使所有 $i \in I$ 的 $j(i)$ 存在；$\supseteq$：全部落在像中则不等号取等），但它的每个输入——$V_i \to Y$ 在 $x_j \mapsto y$ 附近是同构、$f$ 开、$\bigcup_{j(i) = j} V_i \to Y$ 局部有限——都由被引结构给出；④关键追问：本条断言所涉对象（$f, w, d, Y_d$）全部是题面给出的，本证明是造中间装置（指标集 $I$、覆盖 $X = \bigcup_{i \in I} V_i$）去核对断言的性质，而该装置的上游 $T_i$ 又是被引的。合成读法：核心构造被引用 ⇒ 至多 H2；断言里『开』这一半整体外包 ⇒ 按『判整条』条款亦至多 H2。故判 H2（反方向读法见 h3_criterion_note 的留档）。非 ineligible／非 H1：Stacks Project tag 0F3R 的完整作者证明，义务明确（Noetherian 逼近、权重在逆极限下的下降、generic point 处权重比较、以截面像之交刻画最大轨迹），远超通常博士资格考的按定义检查与常规习题，故不判 H1；题证齐备、非开放问题，故非 ineligible。双射／等价条款：本条不是双射或等价断言，不触发该降档条款；识别等式的两个方向仍已逐一核过，降档不来自该条款。

a) 题面与实质要求：curves.tex 行 5537–5548（label=lemma-global-generation，Stacks tag 0E3F）。设 $k$ 为域，$X$ 为 $k$ 上 proper、reduced、connected、维数 $1$ 的概形，$\mathcal{L}$ 为 $X$ 上可逆 $\mathcal{O}_X$-模，假设对每个维数 $1$ 的 reduced connected 闭子概形 $Y \subset X$ 有 $\deg(\mathcal{L}|_Y) \geq 2\dim_k H^1(Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$，则 $\mathcal{L}$ 整体生成。实质义务在于：下界条件只作用在维数 1 的 reduced connected 闭子概形上，$X$ 却允许有多个不可约分支、允许奇异，必须自行造出一条『既约化到某个分支 $Y$、又把 $Y$ 上的整体生成反推回 $X$』的矛盾论证。逐字要求：『Assume that for every reduced connected closed subscheme $Y \subset X$ of dimension $1$ we have $$ \deg(\mathcal{L}|_Y) \geq 2\dim_k H^1(Y, \mathcal{O}_Y) $$ Then $\mathcal{L}$ is globally generated.』（dump 1012–1017）。

b) 允许引用什么（只作起点/归约脚手架，不是结论机制；均点名核过）：Lemma \ref{lemma-degree-more-than-2g}（= curves-lemma-degree-more-than-2g，tag 0E3C，只用于不可约情形的 base case，dump 1022–1025）；有限域时把 $k$ 换成纯超越扩张所引的一串（dump 1026–1035）——Varieties, Lemmas \ref{varieties-lemma-globally-generated-base-change}（0B57）、\ref{varieties-lemma-degree-base-change}（0B59）、\ref{varieties-lemma-geometrically-reduced-any-base-change}（035Z）、\ref{varieties-lemma-bijection-irreducible-components}（038F），Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma \ref{coherent-lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology}（02KH），Lemma \ref{lemma-sanity-check-duality}（= curves-lemma-sanity-check-duality，tag 0E32；同标签亦见 duality-lemma-sanity-check-duality，tag 0FW1，系跨文件重名）；\ref{lemma-vanishing-on-gorenstein}（= curves-lemma-vanishing-on-gorenstein，0E3E；用以得 $H^1(X, \mathcal{L}) = 0$，dump 1064–1065）；\ref{lemma-closed-immersion-dim-1-CM}（= curves-lemma-closed-immersion-dim-1-CM，0E33；用以得 $\omega_Y = \SheafHom(\mathcal{O}_Y, \omega_X)$，dump 1101–1102）；Varieties, Lemma \ref{varieties-lemma-chi-tensor-finite}（0AYT；用以得『support 维数 $0$ 的层由整体截面生成』，dump 1051–1054）。这些被引件没有任何一条给出本条在可约、$k$ 无限情形下的核心断言。

c) 必须由本证明完成的部分（具体做法＋原文定位；行号均为 dump 行）：
(i) 不可约情形整块交出——『If $X$ is irreducible, then the lemma holds by Lemma \ref{lemma-degree-more-than-2g} applied to $X$ viewed as a scheme over the field $k' = H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$.』（dump 1022–1025），有限域替换亦整块交出（dump 1026–1035）。这两处如实记为引用，但它们只是 base case 与预备归约，决定性步骤在 (ii)–(vi)。
(ii) 自造反证装置（dump 1038–1058）：自行选出合用的理想层——『Then we may choose a coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$ such that $H^0(X, \mathcal{I}\mathcal{L}) = H^0(X, \mathcal{L})$ and such that $\mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{I}$ is nonzero with support of dimension $0$. For example, take $\mathcal{I}$ the ideal sheaf of any closed point in the common vanishing locus of the global sections of $\mathcal{L}$.』；再自写短正合列 $0 \to \mathcal{I}\mathcal{L} \to \mathcal{L} \to \mathcal{L}/\mathcal{I}\mathcal{L} \to 0$ 并由长正合列读出『an injection $H^0(X, \mathcal{L}/\mathcal{I}\mathcal{L}) \to H^1(X, \mathcal{I}\mathcal{L})$』。
(iii) 自造『把每个 $\varphi$ 化为零化子条件』的机制（dump 1061–1081，本证明第一处要害）：先写出 $H^1(X, \mathcal{I}\mathcal{L})$ 与 $\Hom(\mathcal{I}\mathcal{L}, \omega_X)$ 的对偶（dump 1061–1063），借被引件的消灭算出 $\dim_k H^0(X, \mathcal{I}\mathcal{L}) = \deg(\mathcal{L}) + \chi(\mathcal{O}_X) > \dim_k H^1(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = \dim_k H^0(X, \omega_X)$（dump 1066–1070），据此断定『We conclude that $\varphi$ is not injective on global sections, in particular $\varphi$ is not injective.』；随即自造对象 $V_\eta \subset \Hom(\mathcal{I}\mathcal{L}, \omega_X)$（在每个不可约分支的一般点 $\eta$ 处为零的那些 $\varphi$，dump 1072–1075），并自行证明『Since every associated point of $\mathcal{I}\mathcal{L}$ is a generic point of $X$, the above shows that $\Hom(\mathcal{I}\mathcal{L}, \omega_X) = \bigcup V_\eta$. (v) 把 (iv) 对每个 $\varphi$ 的分解统一转成上同调的单射（dump 1141–1162）：『Since for every $\varphi$ we have a $\varphi''$ and since $\omega_X \in \textit{Coh}(\mathcal{O}_X)$ represents the functor $\mathcal{F} \mapsto \Hom_k(H^1(X, \mathcal{F}), k)$, we find that $H^1(X, \mathcal{I}\mathcal{L}) \to H^1(Y, \mathcal{I}'\mathcal{L}|_Y)$ is injective.』——即把 (iv) 的『对每个 $\varphi$ 存在 $\varphi''$』读成 $\Hom(\mathcal{I}'\mathcal{L}|_Y, \omega_Y) \to \Hom(\mathcal{I}\mathcal{L}, \omega_X)$ 满，再对偶回收为 $H^1$ 的单射；接上 (ii) 的边界单射，并自证 $H^0(X, \mathcal{L}/\mathcal{I}\mathcal{L}) \to H^0(X, \mathcal{L}|_Y/\mathcal{I}'\mathcal{L}|_Y)$ 是『surjective (and hence bijective)』（dump 1155–1162）。
(vi) 归纳收口（dump 1163–1171）：『But by induction we have that $\mathcal{L}|_Y$ is globally generated (if $Y$ is disconnected this still works of course) and hence the boundary map $$ H^0(X, \mathcal{L}|_Y/\mathcal{I}'\mathcal{L}|_Y) \to H^1(X, \mathcal{I}'\mathcal{L}|_Y) $$ cannot be injective. d) 逐行核过的保真说明：区块完整未截断——STATEMENT 为 dump 1007–1018（12 行 / 424 字节），与 statement_lines=[5537,5548] 精确吻合；PROOF 为 dump 1020–1172（153 行 / 6267 字节含行尾换行），与 proof_lines=[5550,5702] 及 proof_bytes=6266 精确吻合，故两区间四端点自洽。原文写法照抄未改：dump 1041『$H^0(X, \mathcal{I}\mathcal{L}) = H^0(X, \mathcal{L})$』、dump 1056『the fact that $H^0(X, \mathcal{I}\mathcal{L}) = H^0(X, \mathcal{L})$』、dump 1144『represents the functor $\mathcal{F} \mapsto \Hom_k(H^1(X, \mathcal{F}), k)$』、dump 1085『Please keep in mind that the support of $\mathcal{J}$ is $C$.』均按原文照录；另注 $X$ 在题面只假设 reduced，而证明中反复使用 associated point 与 Cohen-Macaulay module（dump 1076、1114），系原文写法，照录不评。

items.title: Uniform Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity bounds for kernels of fixed-rank trivial-sheaf quotients with fixed Hilbert polynomial
items.published_title: Uniform Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity bounds for kernels of fixed-rank trivial-sheaf quotients with fixed Hilbert polynomial
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: Hyperplane induction controls higher cohomology but leaves the first cohomology obstruction unbounded. The proof shows that any nondecreasing step forces all subsequent steps to be injective and hence zero by eventual vanishing, so strict dimension drops and the Hilbert polynomial give a uniform bound.

items.difficulty_reason: The stated proof of Theorem 1.1 (lines 1207--1216) is deliberately a two-line reduction, and the whole weight of the unit sits in the chain it closes over: Lemma 3.5 (source lem4.5) proves that the genus of the critical set at a repeated level is at least l+1, and its proof needs Lemma 3.4 plus Lemma 3.3 (source lem2.161, lines 588--1153), which is a complete source-local compactness machine. Lemma 3.3 has to truncate the L^2-supercritical term to keep I_{mu,tau} bounded below on S_r(c), show that critical points of the truncated functional above a threshold are critical points of the original I_mu, and then establish the (PS)_d condition below level 0 for large mu by estimating the Lagrange multiplier lambda_n finely, invoking the radial concentration-compactness principle at the critical exponent 2*_s, and using the Pohozaev identity to exclude the critical concentration level. Multiplicity then comes from genus theory. items.published_title: Global univalence of the ergodic cylinder transformation on a periodic time scale (Theorem 3.5)
items.author: John M. Davis; Billy J. Jackson; Dylan Poulsen
items.difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the article's central structural result: the averaged map xi-bar_{B^c}, already shown analytic and univalent off the branch cut in the retained Theorem 3.3, is extended across the branch cut B to a globally univalent xi-bar on the whole regressive complex plane. The extension is not a routine continuation, because B is the union of the intervals I_n between consecutive nonregressive points -1/mu_n determined by the graininess spectrum of the time scale. The proof must analyse the monotonicity of gamma_B on each I_n and locate the unique critical point alpha_n where gamma_B' vanishes, then choose interval by interval between xi-bar_{B^c}^+ and its negative so that the resulting piecewise xi-bar_B is injective, and finally verify injectivity across five distinct configurations of points, carrying the argument separately through the case of finitely many graininesses and the case of countably infinitely many. The analytic inputs - Karpuz's analyticity of the complex time-scale exponential and the Noshiro-Warschawski criterion - are named prerequisites supplied by the retained context, so the unit is H2 rather than H3; but the construction of the extension and its case analysis are source-local and are far outside an ordinary qualifying examination in complex analysis or in difference and dynamic equations.

items.difficulty_reason: The counted theorem needs a source-local stability mechanism rather than a routine corollary: the authors dominate the distance functional to the fuzzy zero by a psi-weighted generalized Caputo integral of the delayed right-hand side using assumption (A2), pass to the nondecreasing envelope of the distance to absorb the delay term, verify that the auxiliary functional built on the psi generalized kernel is nondecreasing, and then invoke a generalized Gronwall inequality with the Mittag-Leffler function to convert the explicit solution formula into the quantitative criterion delta times E_{beta,1}(2 L D^beta) not exceeding epsilon. This is a genuine two-sided fuzzy gH-arithmetic estimate for a delay system governed by a psi-generalized Caputo derivative, hence above ordinary PhD qualification exercises, but it stays at estimate-tracking level rather than introducing a new structural mechanism, so it is graded H2 rather than H3.

items.title: Attainment of the nodal Nehari infimum: existence of a least energy sign-changing solution of a Schrodinger system by a four-dimensional Nehari deformation
items.published_title: Attainment of the nodal Nehari infimum: existence of a least energy sign-changing solution of a Schrodinger system by a four-dimensional Nehari deformation
items.author: Anna Lisa Amadori
items.difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the existence half of the main characterization of nodal least energy solutions. After the variational setting, the nodal Nehari manifold and the geometric Lemmas 3.1-3.4 are supplied, the proof still has to control a minimizing sequence on a constraint of codimension four: it must show that the weak limit stays in the set where the nodal and the sign-changing Nehari sets coincide, which requires comparing the nodal level with the decoupled Nehari levels, and then, separately for q equal to 2 and for q larger than 2, construct a four-parameter family that is driven back into the nodal Nehari set, using the two theta-maximisation propositions and the Miranda theorem to produce the sign configuration, and finally derive from the strict decrease of the energy the contradiction that forces the deformation parameter to vanish and the limit to solve the system. This constrained minimax argument with an explicit four-dimensional deformation is research level, not a qualification exercise.

items.title: Pricing callable bonds and optimal callable time under the fractional Black-Scholes market: L1 consistency of the deep-learning price estimator (Theorem 3.6)
items.published_title: Pricing callable bonds and optimal callable time under the fractional Black-Scholes market: L1 consistency of the deep-learning price estimator (Theorem 3.6)
items.author: Yuecai Han, Yinong Wu, Xudong Zheng
items.difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the headline consistency result of the article: the deep-learning estimator of the callable-bond price in a discretised fractional Black-Scholes market converges in L1 to the true price. Its complete proof has to pass from the almost-sure convergence of the discretised expectation by the strong law of large numbers and dominated convergence, rewrite the estimator as an empirical average over the same path grid, isolate the event on which the estimated call time differs from the true one, and then transfer that stopping-time error into a price error by Cauchy-Schwarz against the square-integrability of the discounted payoff, invoking the source-local convergence of the estimated optimal call time. The mechanism is research level because the chain has to control conditional distribution estimators of a fractional-Brownian-motion discrete scheme uniformly in the state, remove the a priori boundedness of the price by a truncation argument and propagate the one-step error backwards through the Bermudan recursion before the final stopping-time comparison is available. It is graded H2 rather than H3 because each ingredient is a quantitative convergence estimate rather than a new structural mechanism: the counted body itself performs the final assembly of prerequisites that the delivered item retains uncounted as complete context.

items.title: Global existence and uniform-in-time boundedness for the 2D chemotaxis-fluid system with double chemical signals under a sub-logistic source (Theorem 1.1)
items.published_title: Global existence and uniform-in-time boundedness for the 2D chemotaxis-fluid system with double chemical signals under a sub-logistic source (Theorem 1.1)
items.author: Shengquan Liu, Dongpu Li, Jiashan Zheng
items.difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the main result of the article: for any real chemotaxis and signal coefficients the two-dimensional chemotaxis-Stokes system with double chemical signals and a sub-logistic source admits a unique global classical solution that is bounded uniformly in time, under an explicit smallness condition coupling the chemical sensitivities, the initial signal bound, the Poincare and Gagliardo-Nirenberg constants and the constant mu that measures the logarithmic sub-logistic growth. The complete proof is a genuine bootstrap: it must extract the L1 bound on the cell density from the sub-logistic source through the infimum representation of the constant M, propagate it to Lp bounds on the velocity through the smoothing of the Stokes equation, obtain the entropy-like estimate for n log n together with the dissipation of the gradients of c, v and u, upgrade to Lp bounds on c and to a gradient estimate on c by the Neumann heat semigroup, and then close the L-infinity bound on n by a Moser-type iteration whose constants only close when the printed smallness condition holds; the extendibility alternative of the local existence lemma converts the resulting uniform bound into global existence. This multi-level a priori bootstrap with sharp constant tracking in a doubly cross-diffusive system is research level, well above an ordinary PhD qualifying examination, so the item is graded H3.

items.title: Infinitely many prescribed-frequency solutions of perturbed Schrodinger-Bopp-Podolsky systems in bounded domains: the critical-point Proposition 3.6
items.published_title: Infinitely many prescribed-frequency solutions of perturbed Schrodinger-Bopp-Podolsky systems in bounded domains: the critical-point Proposition 3.6
items.author: Danilo Gregorin Afonso, Bruno Mascaro
items.difficulty_reason: The counted proposition states that the reduced functional of the perturbed Schrodinger-Bopp-Podolsky system has infinitely many critical points for every prescribed frequency, and it is the source-local step that yields the infinitely many prescribed-frequency solutions asserted by the main theorem of the article. Its complete proof must first record the evenness of the functional and the Palais-Smale property supplied by the source-local compactness lemma, and must then verify the two geometric hypotheses of the symmetric mountain pass theorem in two separate frequency regimes: below half of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue it has to produce a strict local minimum at the origin through a Poincare estimate with an epsilon absorption and the growth conditions on the perturbation, while above that threshold it has to split the space along the eigenvalues of the Dirichlet Laplacian, choose the index at which the frequency crosses the spectrum and prove positivity of the functional on small spheres of the complementary subspace, using the sign of the frequency against that spectral splitting. This is a genuine research-level minimax verification for a fourth-order coupled system; it is graded H2 rather than H3 because the argument applies a named abstract critical point theorem with standard eigenvalue splitting rather than introducing a new compactness or deformation mechanism, the necessary compactness being supplied by the Palais-Smale lemma retained as complete context.

items.title: A quasi-homogeneous Newton-diagram sufficient condition for the real Jacobian conjecture in the plane (Theorem 1.7)
items.published_title: A quasi-homogeneous Newton-diagram sufficient condition for the real Jacobian conjecture in the plane (Theorem 1.7)
items.author: Xiuli Cen, Kangnong Hu, Yuzhou Tian
items.difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the main result of the article: a quasi-homogeneous generalisation of the Newton-diagram sufficient condition for the real Jacobian conjecture in the plane, in which the higher homogeneous terms of the two scalar polynomials are replaced by higher terms with respect to an arbitrary positive weight exponent. Its complete proof must set up the weighted-degree expansion of the squared-norm Hamiltonian, transfer the hypothesis on the two scalar polynomials into a statement about the vanishing set of the highest weighted part, locate the support of the Bendixson-compactified Hamiltonian vector field with respect to the two coordinate axes and the diagonal, split the argument into the two cases in which the first weight is smaller or larger than the second, and in each case identify the Newton diagram vertices and edges, their types and the associated Hamiltonians, and then verify that no associated Hamiltonian carries a factor of the printed special form. The intermediate lemma, which shows that the ordering of the weights forces the highest homogeneous term and the highest term in one variable into a strict sandwich, is what makes the case analysis work. This weighted Newton-diagram analysis in the qualitative theory of polynomial vector fields is research level work, not a qualification exercise, so the item is graded H3.

items.title: The constrained Lojasiewicz-Simon inequality on the unit sphere of a Hilbert space
items.published_title: The constrained Lojasiewicz-Simon inequality on the unit sphere of a Hilbert space
items.author: Zdzisław Brzeźniak, Javed Hussain
items.difficulty_reason: Even with the analytic-gradient-flow background, the source-local Simon theorem and the elliptic regularity of the Dirichlet Laplacian available as context, the counted theorem is not quoted: the author has to derive the Lojasiewicz-Simon inequality on the constraint manifold itself. The proof has to produce an explicit real-analytic chart from the normalisation map Psi together with its analytic inverse Xi, move the constrained functional to the Hilbert space of the tangent plane, identify the reduced gradient through the adjoint A(h) of the chart differential and prove the two-sided norm equivalence between the reduced gradient and the projected H-gradient, verify that the linearisation is the restriction of the second variation and has compact resolvent, invoke the classical Lojasiewicz-Simon theorem in the chart, and only then transfer the chart estimate back to a V-neighbourhood of the stationary point. Deriving a manifold-constrained gradient inequality of this kind is research level, not a qualification exercise.

items.author: Lihong Bao, Libo Wang, Min Li
items.difficulty_reason: After the fractional Sobolev embeddings for the intersection space, the autonomous compactness Lemmas 2.3--2.5 and the non-autonomous compactness Lemma 3.4 are supplied as context, the counted theorem still demands l distinct normalized critical points at negative levels. The author has to run Ekeland variational principle on the L^p mass constraint at each level eta_eps^i, keep the minimizing sequence away from the boundary of the sets theta_eps^i by Lemma 4.2, differentiate along the two-term normalisation path sigma(t) that preserves the mass constraint in order to convert the Ekeland inequality into the constrained Palais-Smale condition, feed the result into the compactness Lemma 3.4 under the strict level bound eta_eps^i < M_max(a)+rho, separate the l limits through the disjoint balls around the maximum points of h, and finally force the Lagrange multipliers to be negative by a Pohozaev-type identity. This normalized-solution multiplicity mechanism under a double (p,q) nonlocality is research level rather than a qualification exercise.

items.published_title: Two nontrivial solutions for a fractional p-Laplacian Kirchhoff problem with steep potential well
items.author: Shuwen He, Shiqing Zhang
items.difficulty_reason: With the fractional Sobolev Lemmas 2.1 and 2.2, the Ekeland-type Theorem 2.4 and the source-local Lemmas 3.1--3.7 together with Remark 3.4, including the truncation compactness Lemma 3.7, available as context, the counted theorem still needs a source-local construction. The author has to build the Cerami sequence of the constrained Kirchhoff functional at the mountain-pass level with the uniform bound on the sequence, apply Lemma 3.7 to obtain convergence for large lambda and small b and small norm of h, then construct the second solution by local minimisation: exhibit a direction along which the functional is negative for small positive multiples, argue that the minimum on the closed ball of radius rho is attained in the open ball, and separate the two levels through a negative value below the mountain-pass level. Controlling the three parameters b, lambda and the norm of h uniformly through the nonlocal Kirchhoff term is beyond a routine qualification problem, although the deepest compactness input is supplied by the retained context.

items.title: Global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions for a viscoelastic coupled system of two wave equations
items.published_title: Global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions for a viscoelastic coupled system of two wave equations
items.author: Houda Fadel, Djamila Benterki, Salim A. Messaoudi
items.difficulty_reason: With Lemmas 2.1 and 2.2, the Poincare and Sobolev tools and the smallness hypothesis on the coupling constant available as context, the counted theorem still requires the whole Faedo-Galerkin construction for a coupled system in which only the first wave equation carries the memory term. The author has to build the approximate solutions on the span of the Dirichlet eigenfunctions, propagate uniform higher-order energy estimates through the memory kernel and through the coupling, extract weakly and weak-star convergent subsequences, identify the limit of the nonlinear memory term, pass the initial data to the limit, and then prove uniqueness by testing the difference of two solutions with the time derivatives of both components and combining Young and Poincare inequalities inside an admissible range of the auxiliary parameter. Well-posedness of this coupled viscoelastic system is a nontrivial research argument rather than a qualification exercise, even though the method is classical.

items.title: Global existence and the uniform a priori estimate in homogeneous Besov spaces for the 2D inviscid magnetic Benard system (Theorem 1.1)
items.published_title: Global existence and the uniform a priori estimate in homogeneous Besov spaces for the 2D inviscid magnetic Benard system (Theorem 1.1)
items.author: Hao Liu; Ruixin Zeng; Chengrong Zhang
items.difficulty_reason: After the paper's Section 2 toolkit (Littlewood--Paley decomposition, Bernstein inequalities, Besov embedding, interpolation and derivative properties, product and commutator estimates) is supplied as context, the counted proof still has to build a source-local mechanism. It must first extract a horizontal dissipation term for the velocity from the temperature equation and a vertical dissipation term from the magnetic equation, through the cancellation identities (3.4), (3.6), (3.7) and (3.8) (source lines 544--609); then combine those four frequency-localized identities with two large constants C1 and C2 into the augmented energy functionals and prove their coercivity against the negative cross terms by Bernstein inequality in the two frequency regimes j at most 0 and j at least -1 (lines 611--666 and 729--777); then sum over the dyadic blocks in the two Besov norms and bound every nonlinear and commutator term by the product of the two energy functionals (lines 677--693 and 850--884); and finally close the Lyapunov-type differential inequality (3.26) under the smallness condition on the supremum of the energy, which is what forces the life span to be infinite by the bootstrap argument (lines 887--908). The named analytic ingredients are classical, but their assembly here is paper-specific and coercivity-free: the dissipation is recovered only from the coupling structure, the two frequency regimes require an induction that is made self-consistent through the constants C1 and C2, and the resulting estimate is uniform in the life span. That is clearly beyond an ordinary PhD qualifying examination on the Euler, Navier--Stokes or MHD equations, and it is graded H2 rather than H3 because each individual ingredient is a named classical estimate rather than a new research device.

items.title: Homogenization in the critical case for an optimal control problem with dynamic boundary conditions on microscopic particles: the homogenized system and the limit adjoint problem (Theorem 5.1)
items.published_title: Homogenization in the critical case for an optimal control problem with dynamic boundary conditions on microscopic particles: the homogenized system and the limit adjoint problem (Theorem 5.1)
items.author: Jesus Ildefonso Diaz; Tatyana A. Shaposhnikova; Alexander V. Podolskiy
items.difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the paper's main homogenization result and its proof is the whole difficulty of the unit. After the setting, the adjoint problem, the a priori estimates and the non-local in time operators of Sections 2 to 4 are supplied as context, the proof must still build a multi-scale construction: it constructs the auxiliary functions solving the model boundary-value problems on the dilated cells (lines 1286--1293) and glues them into the global alternating test functions associated with the controlled and the uncontrolled particles (lines 1298--1313); it applies the surface-to-volume averaging convergence principle (lines 1361--1374) so that the boundary integrals over the particle boundaries of the critical case become volume terms carrying the two thresholds of the limit problem and the strange terms; it then runs four separate passages to the limit for the state equation (Steps A.1 to A.4, lines 1318--1601), where the surfaces of the two particle families must be tracked separately and the limits of the surface terms are identified through the three auxiliary non-local operators; it then repeats the analysis for the adjoint equation (Steps B.1 to B.3, lines 1616--1798), where the combination multiplying the limit adjoint state only collapses to the closed form of the limit operator after the second relation of Lemma 4.1 is used (lines 1657--1671); and it closes by upgrading the subsequence convergences to the whole sequences through the well-posedness of the limit problem (lines 1817--1819). The critical scaling of the radius is exactly what makes the strange terms appear simultaneously in the state equation, in the adjoint equation and in the cost functional, and there is no textbook or qualifying-exam counterpart: each step is a source-local device of this paper. items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the paper's main existence theorem, and its written proof (source lines 1086--1114) is short precisely because it is the top of a source-local chain: the difficulty is the chain, which is delivered in full. Because the nonlinearity is only asymptotically linear, the mountain-pass geometry alone cannot produce a nontrivial solution and the fixed-sign Nehari manifold is not a manifold, so the authors work on the Nehari manifold split into two pieces through the auxiliary function and the map n, and the proof must (i) treat the easy cases through Propositions 3.14 and 3.15, where Ekeland variational principle is legitimised on the constrained set by the lemma preventing the limiting point from reaching the boundary (line 842), and where the concentration-compactness lemma for Palais-Smale sequences together with the norm equivalence turns the weak limit into a strong one (lines 847--850 and 884--895); (ii) in the remaining case, where the barycentric infimum is strictly larger than the limiting level, construct the modified path built from the dilation parameter and the scaling that returns the translated ground state to the Nehari manifold, whose properties are exactly Lemmas 3.16 to 3.20, including the reformulation of hypothesis (A11) as an interval condition and the strict inequality for the path level (lines 1007--1084); and (iii) run a deformation argument on the Nehari manifold to build a continuous map of a ball into its own boundary that is the identity on the boundary, a contradiction of the quoted topological fact (lines 1090--1110), after which sign-definiteness, elliptic regularity and the maximum principle upgrade the critical point to a positive solution (lines 1111--1113). items.title: Global asymptotic stability of the infection equilibrium of a delayed HIV model with CTL immune response and immune impairment (Theorem 3.4)
items.published_title: Global asymptotic stability of the infection equilibrium of a delayed HIV model with CTL immune response and immune impairment (Theorem 3.4)
items.author: Guangsheng Lai; Zhiting Xu
items.difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the paper's strongest dynamical conclusion: the global asymptotic stability of the infection equilibrium of a four-dimensional delayed HIV model that carries a logistic proliferation of target cells, a saturating incidence, an immune-impairment term in the CTL equation and three independent delays. After the well-posedness, the next infection operator, the equilibria and the characteristic-equation results are supplied as context, the proof still has to build a source-local object: the two-part Lyapunov functional N = N_1 + N_2, whose first part is a sum of the fundamental function at the four equilibrium coordinates and whose second part consists of two delay integrals with the correctly weighted integrands (lines 681--695); it then has to differentiate that functional along the flow, insert the four equilibrium identities to replace the production, infection and clearance parameters (lines 733--742), and reduce the resulting expression, by repeated regrouping and by the logarithmic bookkeeping of the fundamental function, to a sum of negative definite squares and of terms of the shape u - 1 - ln u, which is where the strict positivity of the logistic coefficient under the condition $x_{\rm max}(r-d) < r x^{*}$ is used (lines 744--827); and it must then identify the largest invariant subset of the zero set of the derivative and invoke LaSalle invariance to conclude (lines 828--834). The method is classical but its execution is entirely paper-specific: the weights of the delay integrals and the cancellation pattern have to be found, and the reduction is a long non-obvious algebraic chain that no qualifying examination would ask for, so the unit is graded H2 rather than H3 because every ingredient is a named classical device rather than a new research mechanism.

【题面逐字（dump:1473–1488）】\begin{lemma}
\label{lemma-desingularize}
Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring.
Let $\Lambda$ be an $R$-algebra. Let $\pi \in R$ and
assume that $\text{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi) = \text{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi^2)$. Let
$A \to \Lambda$ be an $R$-algebra map with $A$ of finite
presentation. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item the image of $\pi$ is strictly standard in $A$ over $R$, and
\item there exists a section $\rho : A/\pi^4 A \to R/\pi^4 R$
which is compatible with the map to $\Lambda/\pi^4 \Lambda$.
\end{enumerate}
Then we can find $R$-algebra maps $A \to B \to \Lambda$ with $B$
of finite presentation such that $\mathfrak a B \subset H_{B/R}$ where
$\mathfrak a = \text{Ann}_R(\text{Ann}_R(\pi^2)/\text{Ann}_R(\pi))$.
\end{lemma}

【实质要求】断言的是一个存在性：在假设 (1)「$\pi$ 的像在 $A$ 上对 $R$ 严格标准」与 (2)「存在截面 $\rho : A/\pi^4A \to R/\pi^4R$ 且与到 $\Lambda/\pi^4\Lambda$ 的映射相容」下，造出 $R$-代数映射 $A \to B \to \Lambda$，$B$ 有限展示，且 $\mathfrak a B \subset H_{B/R}$（$\mathfrak a = \text{Ann}_R(\text{Ann}_R(\pi^2)/\text{Ann}_R(\pi))$）。这里 $H_{B/R}$ 是同章定义的奇异理想（源 definition-singular-ideal：$V(H_{B/R}) = \{\mathfrak q \mid R \to B$ 在 $\mathfrak q$ 不光滑$\}$ 的唯一根理想）。所以实质要求＝造一个 $\pi$-进加厚 $B$，把「$A$ 上 $\pi$ 的几乎光滑性」（严格标准 ⇒ $A_\pi$ 光滑，且模 $\pi^4$ 有截面）抬成「$B$ 在 $\mathfrak a$ 之外处处光滑」。注意题面只给「截面存在」这一输入，其来源（在应用中由 lemma-lifting 供给，源 1887）不在本条职责内——本条是把该输入用足，不是把它造出来。

f) 为何仍判 H2（逐条回应第 (iii) 条，并给出 (ii) 的评估）。(1) 本条是参考书（Stacks 章 smoothing）里的工具引理，标签本身即 lemma-helper，唯一消费者是另一条引理证明里的一步（2584），而该引理又只是本节（导语只声明解释不可分剩余域情形下如何解局部问题）的工具，再经 2624/2672 通向本章冠名主定理 Theorem [Popescu]（3112–3115）：不属『某节冠名的主定理或同等地位的结果』。(2) 机制按其实质是全套标准件的组合，证明内自造物（$\sigma$、$\Psi_\sigma$、$A = F[x]/(x)^n$、$\tau$、$\theta$、$D$、$\xi$、$f_j$）是记账对象而非有独立地位的新对象：① 幂零指数归纳（2459–2461『Let $n$ be the minimal integer such that $\mathfrak m^n = 0$. / We will prove this lemma by induction on $n$.』、2480–2482）；② 形式光滑给系数型截面（2464–2468、2497，由被引件交付）；③ 用剩余域上的多项式环表示 Artinian 局部代数 $\Psi_\sigma$（2469–2473）；④『两个模幂零理想同余的截面之差是导子』（2498–2501）——形变论标准事实，且同语料多章复用『截面可加导子』手法（algebra.tex、crystalline.tex、defos.tex、formal-defos.tex、more-algebra.tex 等均出现 derivation $D$）；⑤ $\sigma \mapsto \sigma + D$、$\theta \mapsto \theta - D|_k$ 的挠作用（2490–2491、2502–2503）；⑥ Jacobi–Zariski 正合性 ＋ 假设 $\dim H_1 < \infty$ ⇒ 有限 $J_0$（2513–2516）——余切/余法丛技术；⑦ 用 $\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}$ 的泛性质把 $\theta - D|_k$ 分解为 $\xi \circ \text{d}$（2517–2524）；⑧ 有限生成记账：扩 $F'$ 为 $F = F'(c_{j,E})$（2529–2533）、再并入 $g_1, \ldots, g_t$ 的系数（2536–2539『and we may assume their / coefficients are in $F$ after enlarging $F$ by adjoining finitely many / elements』）；⑨ 平坦性 2540–2542『In this case it is clear that the map / $A = F[x_1, \ldots, x_d]/(g_1, \ldots, g_t) \to / K[x_1, \ldots, x_d]/(g_1, \ldots, g_t) = \Lambda$ is flat.』——沿域扩张作基变换（$K$ 是有限自由 $F$-模的滤过余极限，滤过余极限保持平坦），原文按 clear 处理。(3) (ii) 只勉强成立：结论是研究级机器（André–Quillen 同调、形式光滑、Artinian 局部代数的滤过余极限表示）下的存在性陈述，但其分量从属于 2584 的一步，不具奠基性，也非本章冠名成果。(4) 结论：判 H2。如实记录分歧点：本条 (i) 成立，且『用 $\dim H_1(L_{K/k}) < \infty$ 造校正导子』不可由任何被引命题取得，故它是 H2 偏上的边缘判例；压到 H2 的依据是第 (iii) 条的工具引理条款（机制全用标准件、无有独立地位的新对象或新机制）与 (ii) 的分量从属，按『判低不判高、如实判低优于硬抬』取 H2。

items.difficulty_reason: The existence proof has to control random extractor evaluations that overlap across several noncolluding tampering functions, so its main concentration argument cannot assume independent samples. The authors build a bounded-degree collision graph, partition its seeds into independent classes, and establish the conditional mean-zero property needed for separate martingale bounds on both the joint and product-distribution distinguishers. Their complete human core then performs the simultaneous source, adversary and test-function union bound with explicit entropy and seed-length costs; the difficulty is this new dependency-control construction rather than a routine random-function count.

The counted proof has to build the group I(Y,E,sigma;R) as a quotient of the direct sum over all regular perturbations carrying the signature datum sigma by the canonical isomorphisms rho_12 defined by paths of perturbations, verify that each inclusion of a summand is an isomorphism onto the quotient, prove that the chain map induced by a cobordism is independent of the regular perturbation extending the boundary data, and then check composition up to chain homotopy so that the construction really is a functor on the weakly admissible U(2)-cobordism category. items.title: Transience of the zero set of a polynomial evaluated on the symplectic representation of the braid group
items.published_title: Transience of the zero set of a polynomial evaluated on the symplectic representation of the braid group
items.author: Marc Soret and Marina Ville
items.difficulty_reason: Once the classical inputs are supplied as named prerequisites - A’Campo’s surjectivity of B(n+1) onto Sp(2l,F_p), Diaconis’s convergence criterion for a random walk on a finite group generated as a semigroup by its support, Aschbacher’s simplicity of PSp(2n,F_p), the Lachaud-Rolland point-count bound for algebraic sets over finite fields and the irreducibility of Sp(2l,K) as an algebraic variety - the counted proof still has to assemble a source-local transience theorem for the zero set of an arbitrary integer polynomial on the symplectic representation, which is not a qualification exercise. The author must reduce the braid walk to a walk on the finite group Sp(2l,F_p) through the reduction map Pi_p, verify both Diaconis hypotheses for Sp(2l,F_p) including the exceptional case l=1, p=3 by an explicit computation with the reduced Burau images s_1, s_2 and the complete list of normal subgroups of SL(2,F_3), bound the density of the zero set P_p^{-1}(0) inside Sp(2l,F_p) by combining the order formula for Sp(2l,F_p) with the Lachaud-Rolland estimate on a proper subvariety of dimension at most 2l^2+l-1, and then run the epsilon argument that converts the finite-field density bound into the vanishing, as k tends to infinity, of the probability that the walk hits the zero set at step k. That combination - finite-group equidistribution for a Zariski-dense subgroup image together with a Lang-Weil-type density estimate transferred to a random walk on a braid group - is research-level probability and arithmetic geometry, well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations.

items.published_title: The Rank Property of Thin Slabs: exact rank at most 2b for the far-field blocks of the reduced slab-interface matrix
items.author: Anna Yesypenko, Per-Gunnar Martinsson
items.difficulty_reason: The counted proof is the article’s own theoretical justification of the two-level solver and is not a qualification exercise. Starting from the Schur complement T_11 = A_11 - A_12 A_22^{-1} A_21 of the slab-ordered five-point stencil, the author must exhibit the block LDU factorization of the sparse banded matrix A_22, propagate the sparsity pattern of A_F2 and A_2B through the triangular factors U_22^{-1} and L_22^{-1} to obtain the factorizations X_F2 = [A_Fa 0 A_Fg] U_22^{-1} and Y_2B = L_22^{-1} [0; A_bB; A_gB], conclude that the compensation term X_Fg Y_gB has exact rank |J_gamma| = 2b because the middle column block of X_F2 vanishes identically, and finally separate the sparse O(1)-entry part A_FB from that rank-2b part, with the symmetric argument for (T_11)_BF. items.published_title: Approximability estimate of balanced group convolution: the K(1-1/N)^3 bound for the optimal intergroup error
items.author: Youngkyu Lee, Jongho Park, Chang-Ock Lee
items.difficulty_reason: Supplying the article's own prerequisites - the block matrix form of a standard convolution, the group convolution, the definition of the balanced group convolution with its intergroup mean, the approximability functional, Assumptions 3.1 and 3.2, the Young-type inequality of Lemma 3.3 and the K/n improvement of Lemma 3.4, both with complete proofs, and the whole of Theorem 3.5 with its proof - still leaves a source-local assembly that is not a qualification exercise. The counted proof has to build the balancing term from the intergroup mean, verify that the balanced group convolution reproduces the standard convolution up to the group-diagonal part, decompose the residual into one summand per group of the form \|\sum_{l != k} \bW^{kl} (\bx^l - \bar{\bx})\|^2, re-run the group-convolution estimate of Theorem 3.5 with the centred channels \bx^l - \bar{\bx} in place of the channels \bx^l (using that the independence of the input coordinates was never used there), and then convert the centred norm through the exact identity \bbE[\|\bar{\bx}\|^2] = N^{-2}\bbE[\|\bx\|^2] + ((N-1)/N)\|\bbE[\bx^1]\|^2 into the extra (1-1/N) factor, carrying the two assumption regimes C_{n,N,k} = K and C_{n,N,k} = K/(n-n/N) through to the two constants K(1-1/N)^3 and (K/n)(1-1/N)^2. items.title: The divergence-graph edge algorithm for equal-length horocyclic suffixes: linear-time certification of close successors and computation of the uncancelable clique by a finite-state machine
items.published_title: The divergence-graph edge algorithm for equal-length horocyclic suffixes: linear-time certification of close successors and computation of the uncancelable clique by a finite-state machine
items.author: Noah Jillson, Daniel N. Levitin, Pramana Saldin, Katerina Stuopis, Qianruixi Wang, Kaicheng Xue
items.difficulty_reason: The counted proof is the paper's own correctness argument for the finite-state machine that decides divergence-graph edges between horocyclic suffixes of equal length, and it is not a qualification exercise. Even with the standing assumptions, the horocyclic normal form of Section 5.1 and the cancellation lemmas of Section 5.2 supplied, the author has to build the state - the subwords u_1, u_2 and u_3, u_4 (or u_5, u_6) of the two horocyclic suffixes, the clique K of uncancelable letters, the bit b recording which word owns the cancelable letters, and the two subword indices n_w and n_v - and then verify five interlocking update rules: the index update, the bit flip forced when one word has moved on to a later subword, the adding letter, the processing of the canceling letter together with the deletion of the letters that it forbids, and the closing bit-flip check. The mathematical content is the invariant maintained across those rules, that K is always a clique commuting with every surviving subword, and the two-sided conclusion: any failure of a check is exactly a pair of uncancelable letters, while a successful run computes K(v,w), the word of cancelable letters, and the side of the pair on which that word must be written. Nothing here is a textbook computation: it is the paper's own reduction of the geometry of the divergence graph to a finite automaton over the horocyclic normal form, and it is what makes the article's later linear-time and O(n log n) generation theorems work. This is research-level geometric group theory and automata over Coxeter groups, well beyond an ordinary PhD qualifying examination.

items.title: Safety from exponential matrix control barrier functions
items.published_title: Safety from exponential matrix control barrier functions
items.author: Pio Ong, Yicheng Xu, Ryan M. Bena, Faryar Jabbari, Aaron D. Ames
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the article's Theorem 1 (source label thm:EMCBF-safety), the safety theorem of the matrix control barrier function framework: if H is an exponential MCBF then the safe set defined by the matrix inequality H(x) >= 0 is control invariant and the semidefinite-programming safety filter CBF-SDP is continuous on a neighborhood of the safe set. The unit is not a qualification exercise because the counted claim cannot be reached without the whole source-local framework that the unit retains: the matrix-valued barrier condition with its entry-wise Lie derivative matrix and the auxiliary scalarized function argument proving forward invariance (Proposition 1 and its complete proof), the exponential MCBF definition with its strict matrix inequality, and the proof of the counted theorem itself, which constructs the feasible set as a set-valued map, identifies it with a sublevel set of the minimum-eigenvalue function, uses global Lipschitzness of the eigenvalue function on symmetric matrices, and then invokes lower semicontinuity of a convex-valued map with nonempty interior together with the continuity of the minimal selection of a closed convex-valued lower semicontinuous map to obtain continuity of the safety filter before closing the argument with the matrix barrier condition. The retained uncounted Proposition 2 with its own complete proof adds the nonsmooth eigenvalue bound obtained from the generalized gradient through Caratheodory's theorem for convex hulls and the comparison lemma. Combining matrix inequalities and semidefinite programming with set-valued analysis and nonsmooth eigenvalue analysis into a new safety framework is research-level control theory, well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations.

items.title: Uniqueness of transonic shock solutions modulo a translation in an approximate nozzle
items.published_title: Uniqueness of transonic shock solutions modulo a translation in an approximate nozzle
items.author: Minghong Han, Bingsong Long, Hairong Yuan
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the article's main theorem, published as Theorem 1.1 (Main theorem): for given uniform supersonic inflow, the free boundary problem for the steady potential flow equation (an elliptic-hyperbolic mixed type equation) on the sphere has a transonic shock solution if and only if the exit speed equals the constant u_1 determined by the data, and that solution is unique modulo a translation of the shock. The unit is not a qualification exercise because the counted claim cannot be reached without the whole source-local analysis that the unit retains and that the proof body carries: the reduction of the flow to a Cauchy problem for a nonlinear ordinary differential equation by Bernoulli's law, the construction of the symmetric background solution and the proof that its shock location is not determined (the chain rule computation through the Rankine-Hugoniot conditions, equation (2.6) and the identity (2.8)), the linearisation of the mass conservation equation about the background solution with its uniformly elliptic coefficient matrix and the first-order terms, the boundary conditions on the exit and on the shock, the sign claim psi <= 0 on the shock obtained by integrating the difference of the two background velocity fields, and then the global argument itself: the strong maximum principle with the Hopf boundary point lemma in the two cases u_1 >= c_theta_1 and u_1 < c_theta_1, including the normal-derivative contradiction at a minimum on the shock, whose justification is deferred to Remark 2.4 and carried out there by a second integral comparison. Proving uniqueness modulo translation for a transonic shock free boundary problem in a curved approximate nozzle is research-level nonlinear partial differential equations, well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations.

items.author: Pawe{\l} St{\c{e}}pniak, Zbigniew Palmowski

items.published_title: First-order asymptotic expansion of a simple real transmission eigenvalue of a periodic scatterer of bounded support
items.author: Fioralba Cakoni and Shari Moskow
items.difficulty_reason: The counted proof is the article's own deduction of its main theorem - the first-order asymptotic expansion of a simple real transmission eigenvalue of a periodically oscillating scatterer of bounded support - from the Osborn-type nonlinear eigenvalue perturbation theorem that the article states as Theorem 1 and from the fourth-order homogenization estimates it proves. Even with the whole preceding apparatus available in the delivered context (the variational fourth-order reformulation of the interior transmission eigenvalue problem, the two-scale asymptotics with the cell problems for chi, gamma, alpha and B, the boundary correctors theta_eps^{(n)}, Lemma 2 on their L^2 boundedness, Propositions 1-2 and Corollary 2 giving the O(eps) operator estimate, Theorem 1 quoted from Osborn's theory, and the computed denominator (81) and numerator (82)), the counted proof is a source-local research argument rather than a qualification exercise: one must pass from the L^2 estimate of (T_eps(tau)-T_0(tau))f by C_tau eps to strong pointwise convergence of the operators uniformly on bounded regions of the complex plane, using the explicit coercivity of the fourth-order operator to make the constant tau-independent; one must establish collective compactness of the family T_eps(tau) from the uniform H^2 bound on u_eps = T_eps(tau)f; one must recognise that the hypotheses of the quoted perturbation theorem are met and that, because the eigenspace R(E) is one-dimensional here, the remainder on the right-hand side of its expansion is O(eps^2); and one must insert the article's own denominator (81) and numerator (82) into that expansion to obtain the explicit correction formula, in which the leading microstructure effect is the fourth-order boundary corrector theta_eps^{(2)} integrated against the scaled eigenfunction, under the explicit solvability condition that L^{-1}_{tau_0,0} phi paired with phi differs from (nbar-3)/(2 tau_0 nbar). Identifying that the boundary corrector, and not the bulk corrector, dominates the correction, and assembling the hypothesis chain (sign-definite contrast, simple homogenized eigenvalue, H^5 regularity of the eigenfunction) is research-level homogenization reasoning beyond ordinary PhD qualification problems in analysis.

items.published_title: Manifold traversal of next-token decoding trajectories: a smooth simplex trajectory converging to the softmax equilibrium
items.author: Christopher R. Lee-Jenkins
items.difficulty_reason: The counted proof is the author's own proof of the paper's advertised main result, the manifold-traversal theorem for next-token decoding, and it is not a qualification exercise: given the paper's own ingredients in the delivered context (the Gibbs variational characterisation of the softmax as the unique maximiser of the strictly concave free energy, the entropic mirror step with its multiplicative-weights solution, the replicator ODE as the continuous-time limit, the forward-invariance lemma for the replicator field, and the energy-ascent proposition), the counted proof must still assemble a three-part dynamical argument on the open probability simplex: it must convert forward invariance of the faces plus smoothness of the replicator field on the relative interior into existence and uniqueness of a global C^1 solution that never leaves the interior; it must transfer the free-energy ascent of the mirror/replicator step to the flow so that the free energy is a Lyapunov function with strict increase off the stationary set; and it must identify the stationary points of the flow with the KKT conditions of the variational problem in order to conclude that the unique interior stationary point is the softmax equilibrium, then invoke LaSalle's invariance principle, together with the boundedness of the free energy above by its value at the equilibrium, to upgrade Lyapunov ascent to convergence of every interior trajectory to that equilibrium. items.title: Internal Categoricity and the Generic Multiverse: the consistency of a non-standard model of $MV$ all of whose worlds are uncountable and transitive (Proposition 10)
items.published_title: Internal Categoricity and the Generic Multiverse: the consistency of a non-standard model of $MV$ all of whose worlds are uncountable and transitive (Proposition 10)
items.author: Toby Meadows
items.difficulty_reason: The counted proposition is the consistency, from the hypothesis that $L_{\omega_1}$ satisfies ZFC, of a non-standard model of the generic multiverse all of whose worlds are uncountable and transitive, and it is carried by the longest single argument of the paper: a 117-line forcing proof, longer than the 78-line proof of Theorem 13 and the 69-line proof of Theorem 29. The proof has to build the model rather than quote one. It introduces Silver's collapse forcing $\mathbb{S}_X$ with its first and second domains, explains how it differs from Levy's collapse $\mathbb{C}_{\omega_1}$ through the countable completeness of its second domain, handles the metamathematical point that such a generic need not exist by working virtually under $\Vdash_{\mathbb{S}_{\omega_1}}$ inside $L$, states and proves a two-part claim inside the proof (part (1) that every set in $[\omega_1]^{\omega_1}\cap V[H]$ has a countably infinite subset in $L$, by a descending sequence of conditions chosen with least second domain and a fusion-style bound, and part (2) that a $\mathbb{C}_{\omega_1}$-generic $G$ yields a set with no countably infinite subset in $L$), defines the name $\dot A$ from conditions acting on $0$, recalls the abstract weak-density transfer fact for order-preserving maps, embeds $\mathbb{C}_{\omega_1}$ weakly densely into $Add(\omega_1,1)$ through $\sigma(p)(\alpha)=1$ iff $p(0,\alpha)=1$, and closes with the finite-condition argument. None of this is examined at the level of an ordinary PhD qualifying examination, where forcing appears as the standard Cohen and Levy collapse together with the definability, chain-condition and truth lemmas; here the candidate must construct a new consistency model, control two different collapsing forcings at once and carry a fusion argument inside a claim embedded in the proof. With the paper's own section 2 retained as context, so that the axioms of $MV$ and the prerequisites are supplied, the unit still stands well above the bar: H3.

items.published_title: A Note on Distance-Fall Colorings: the distance-2 fall 3-colouring theorem (Theorem 2.1)
items.author: Wayne Goddard and Sonwabile Mafunda
items.difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the note's headline result and its short proof is a minimal-counterexample argument that is not available from any standard textbook. items.author: Tomasz Kania and Jaros{\l}aw Swaczyna

items.author: Mark Van Raamsdonk
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the paper's Fourier-coefficient criterion for the safe functions on a hypergraph, printed as Lemma 4.2 (source0.tex lines 557--560), delivered together with the paper's complete original proof of it at source0.tex lines 571--621. The preparation note for this item paired that fifty-one-line proof block with the theorem that follows the lemma, and it is worth correcting, because the block's own first line is a proof environment carrying the annotation (Lemma FourLemma) and FourLemma is the label of the lemma at source0.tex line 558. The theorem printed immediately after the lemma, Theorem 4.3, has no proof of its own: the paper says only that it follows by the same logic as the proof of its earlier graph-theoretic Fourier theorem. The counted unit is therefore the lemma, and the fifty-one-line block is the paper's own complete proof of it. The proof is a self-contained Boolean-cube argument. It fixes an intersection I and a bipartition of I, writes the safety condition (13) in the Fourier basis as the vanishing of a sum against the test function g of the bipartition (14), and computes the inner product of g with each Fourier character. For any vertex outside I the contributing sets come in complementary pairs obtained by toggling that vertex, and the two terms cancel whenever the vertex lies in the character's index set, so the inner product can be nonzero only for index sets contained in I; on those sets the contributing terms are exactly the sets of the form a union phi and b union phi with phi disjoint from I, and after factoring out the common characters the sum evaluates to a two-term expression whose bracket vanishes exactly when the parity conditions on a and b agree with the index set. That reduces the whole safety condition to the system (15) over even-order subsets of I. The paper then counts the system: one equation per bipartition, that is one fewer than the number of unknowns, and it proves independence rather than assuming it. Fixing a distinguished element of I, parametrising bipartitions by the nonempty subsets of the remaining set, and introducing the bijection that turns an arbitrary subset into an even-order subset by adjoining the distinguished element when the order is odd, it rewrites the system as the vanishing of a function on the remaining Boolean cube against every nonempty point (16), and concludes from the invertibility of the Fourier basis there that all the coefficients attached to even-order subsets of I are equal. That is precisely the statement. The argument is not an exercise: it requires the cancellation-by-complementary-pairs step, the parity reduction, and the change of variables that turns the system into a Fourier-invertibility statement, and none of these is a routine verification of a definition. It is the paper's own technical core, its result is what the theorem printed immediately after it is deduced from, and no qualifying examination poses it, which places it in the upper qualifying-to-research range: H2.

items.title: Random domain decomposition for parabolic PDEs on graphs: the convergence theorem (Theorem 2.3)
items.published_title: Random domain decomposition for parabolic PDEs on graphs: the convergence theorem (Theorem 2.3)
items.author: Mart\'in Hern\'andez
items.difficulty_reason:
Counted unit: the paper's convergence theorem for the continuous random batch method, printed as Theorem 2.3 of the paper (source0.tex lines 331--337; the environment carries the optional title Convergence and the source label th:convergence), delivered together with the paper's own complete proof of it at source0.tex lines 675--1128. The statement is that for the parabolic problem on the graph, its random-batch approximation and the randomized coefficients, the quantity Lambda measuring the variance of the randomization is uniformly bounded in the batch step size and the mean-square error between the two solutions is bounded, uniformly in time, by a constant times the square root of the L1 norm of Lambda times the step size h, with a constant independent of h. It is the paper's main result: the abstract advertises exactly this first-order mean-square convergence of the random batch method at the level of the partial differential equation, without any preliminary discretization in space or time.

The author's proof is complete and extends over roughly four hundred and fifty lines of the source. The author forms the difference of the two solutions, differentiates its squared L2 norm on each randomization interval, decomposes the resulting bilinear expression into the four groups of terms produced by the randomized coefficients, the randomized source and the randomized interval selection, and estimates each group separately: the leading terms are absorbed into the unperturbed energy identity, the remaining ones are bounded by Cauchy-Schwarz, by the boundedness of the coefficients and by the definition of Lambda, and the sums over the random batches are replaced by their expectations using the exchangeability of the batches. The resulting differential inequality is closed by Gronwall's lemma, which produces a bound with an exponential factor in the final time, and the last step converts the surviving double integral of the time derivative of the random solution into a single factor of the step size by first proving an absolute-continuity estimate for the random solution, and then invokes the energy estimate of the paper's well-posedness theorem for the random system to bound the remaining norm by a constant that is independent of h. The proof therefore depends on the paper's own maximal-regularity theorem, on the well-posedness theorem for the random system, on the boundedness lemma for Lambda, and on the whole machinery of the randomized decomposition, all of which are retained in the delivered document.

Carrying this out requires, beyond the standard energy method for parabolic problems, the randomization of a domain decomposition with a non-overlapping cover of the graph, the correct splitting of the consistency error into the terms that can be absorbed and the terms that must be paid for by Lambda, the interchange of the expectation with the time integral over a random number of intervals, and the careful tracking of the constants so that none of them depends on the step size. No qualifying examination poses this: the argument is the technical core of a research paper on random domain decomposition for partial differential equations on graphs, it is stated for a general graph with piecewise smooth coefficients and boundary data, and the constant is required to be uniform in the batch step size. That places the unit in the research range: H3.
